title.zh: 卷五十 列傳第四十四 文學下
title.raw: 卷五十 列傳第四十四 文學下 Volume 50: Men of Letters 2

sentences.zh: 劉峻 劉沼 謝幾卿 劉勰 王籍 何思澄 劉杳 謝徵 臧嚴 伏挺 庾仲容 陸雲公 任孝恭 顏協

translations.literal: Liu Jun, Liu Zhao, Xie Jiqing, Liu Xie, Wang Ji, He Sichen, Liu Yao, Xie Zheng, Zang Yan, Fu Ting, Yu Zhongrong, Lu Yungong, Ren Xiaogong, Yan Xie
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun · Liu Zhao · Xie Jiqing · Liu Xie · Wang Ji · He Sichen · Liu Yao · Xie Zheng · Zang Yan · Fu Ting · Yu Zhongrong · Lu Yungong · Ren Xiaogong · Yan Xie

sentences.zh: 劉峻字孝標，平原平原人。

translations.literal: Liu Jun, courtesy name Xiaobiao, was a man of Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun, styled Xiaobiao, came from Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父珽，宋始興內史。

translations.literal: His father Ting was Song Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ting was Song administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 峻生期月，母攜還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Jun was one month old his mother took him back to their home district.
translations.idiomatic: At one month Jun's mother carried him home to the district.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，青州陷魏，峻年八歲，爲人所略至中山，中山富人劉實湣峻，以束帛贖之，教以書學。

translations.literal: At the start of Song's Taishi era Qing province fell to Wei; Jun was eight and was carried off to Zhongshan, where the wealthy Liu Shi of Zhongshan pitied him, ransomed him with silk, and taught him letters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song Taishi Qingzhou fell to Wei; eight-year-old Jun was seized to Zhongshan, ransomed by the rich Liu Shi, and taught to read.

sentences.zh: 魏人聞其江南有戚屬，更徙之桑乾。

translations.literal: When the northerners heard he had kin in the south they moved him again to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing he had southern kin, the Wei moved him again to Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 峻好學，家貧，寄人廡下，自課讀書，常燎麻炬，從夕達旦，時或昏睡，爇其發，旣覺復讀，終夜不寐，其精力如此。

translations.literal: Jun loved learning; his family was poor and he lodged under others' eaves, setting his own lessons, often burning hemp torches from dusk to dawn; when he dozed he singed his hair, and waking read on all night without sleep—such was his zeal.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and lodging in a lean-to, he studied by hemp torch till dawn, singeing his hair when he dozed, then reading on sleepless—such was his zeal.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，從桑乾得還，自謂所見不博，更求異書，聞京師有者，必往祈借，清河 崔慰祖謂之「書淫」。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming he returned from Sanggan, felt his reading was not broad enough, and sought rare books; hearing any in the capital he would go beg to borrow—Cui Weizu of Qinghe called him a "book lecher."
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi Yongming he came back from Sanggan, sought rare books, and borrowed whatever the capital held—Cui Weizu of Qinghe dubbed him a book lecher.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵王子良博招學士，峻因人求爲子良國職，吏部尚書徐孝嗣抑而不許，用爲南海王侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: When Prince Ziliang of Jingling widely recruited scholars Jun asked through someone to be a princely retainer; Minister of Personnel Xu Xiaosi blocked it and he was offered Southern Sea prince attendant—he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling recruited widely; Jun sought a post but Xu Xiaosi blocked it; offered Southern Sea attendant, he refused.

sentences.zh: 至明帝時，蕭遙欣爲豫州，爲府刑獄，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Under Mingdi Xiao Yaoxin was Inspector of Yuzhou; Jun served as prison officer of the princedom and was treated very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingdi he was prison officer for Xiao Yaoxin, inspector of Yuzhou, and was honored lavishly.

sentences.zh: 遙欣尋卒，久之不調。

translations.literal: Yaoxin soon died; for a long time Jun received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxin soon died; long afterward he still had no post.

sentences.zh: 天監初，召入西省，與學士賀蹤典校秘書。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was summoned to the Western Office and with the scholar He Zong collated the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he entered the Western Office and with He Zong collated secret books.

sentences.zh: 峻兄孝慶，時爲青州刺史，峻請假省之，坐私載禁物，爲有司所奏，免官。

translations.literal: Jun's elder brother Xiaoqing was then Inspector of Qingzhou; Jun asked leave to visit him, was charged with privately carrying forbidden goods, impeached, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xiaoqing was Qingzhou inspector; Jun visited on leave, was charged with smuggling forbidden goods, and lost office.

sentences.zh: 安成王秀好峻學，及遷荊州，引爲戶曹參軍，給其書籍，使抄錄事類，名曰《類苑》。

translations.literal: Prince Xiu of Ancheng loved Jun's learning; when moved to Jingzhou he made him household registrar, supplied books, and had him copy topics into a work called Garden of Categories.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Ancheng prized his learning, made him registrar at Jingzhou, supplied books, and had him compile the Garden of Categories.

sentences.zh: 未及成，復以疾去，因游東陽紫岩山，築室居焉。

translations.literal: Before it was finished he left again on illness, traveled to Purple Rock Mountain in Dongyang, and built a dwelling there.
translations.idiomatic: Ill again before it was done, he withdrew to Purple Rock in Dongyang and built a house.

sentences.zh: 爲《山栖志》，其文甚美。

translations.literal: He wrote Mountain Dwelling Record, a very fine piece.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Mountain Dwelling Record, a work of great beauty.

sentences.zh: 高祖招文學之士，有高才者，多被引進，擢以不次。

translations.literal: Gaozu recruited men of letters; those of high talent were often brought in and promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned literary talent and often promoted the gifted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 峻率性而動，不能隨衆沉浮，高祖頗嫌之，故不任用。

translations.literal: Jun acted from native bent and could not drift with the crowd; Gaozu rather disliked this and so did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Frank and unable to float with the crowd, he was disliked by Gaozu and never used.

sentences.zh: 乃著《辨命論》以寄其懷曰：

translations.literal: He then wrote Discourse on Destiny to lodge his feelings, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote Discourse on Destiny to voice his mind, saying:

sentences.zh: 主上嘗與諸名賢言及管輅，歎其有奇才而位不達。

translations.literal: Our lord once spoke with famous worthies of Guan Lu and sighed that such rare talent had not reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once discussed Guan Lu with eminent men and lamented that genius had not won rank.

sentences.zh: 時有在赤墀之下，預聞斯議，歸以告余。

translations.literal: Someone below the Red Steps heard this talk, returned, and told me.
translations.idiomatic: Someone on the red steps who heard it told me on returning.

sentences.zh: 余謂士之窮通，無非命也。

translations.literal: I say that whether a gentleman meets obstruction or success is nothing but fate.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that a scholar's rise or fall is all fate.

sentences.zh: 故謹述天旨，因言其略云。

translations.literal: Therefore I respectfully set forth Heaven's intent and state the outline thus:
translations.idiomatic: So I respectfully follow Heaven's meaning and sketch the argument:

sentences.zh: 臣觀管輅天才英偉，珪璋特秀，實海內之髦傑，豈日者卜祝之流。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that Guan Lu's heaven-given brilliance was outstanding, jade-scepter excellence singular—a true hero within the seas, no mere day-reader or prayer-officiant.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu was brilliantly gifted and peerless—a true hero of the realm, no common diviner.

sentences.zh: 而官止少府丞，年終四十八，天之報施，何其寡歟？

translations.literal: Yet his office stopped at Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and he died at forty-eight—how meager Heaven's reward!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he only reached vice director of the palace storehouse and died at forty-eight—how scant Heaven's reward!

sentences.zh: 然則高才而無貴仕，饕餮而居大位，自古所歎，焉獨公明而已哉？

translations.literal: Thus high talent without noble office and gluttons in great posts have been lamented since antiquity—why only Gongming?
translations.idiomatic: High talent without rank and gluttons in high place have long been lamented—not Guan Lu alone.

sentences.zh: 故性命之道，窮通之數，夭閼紛綸，莫知其辨。

translations.literal: Hence the way of nature and life, the reckoning of rise and fall, early death and blockage are tangled—none knows their distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Life, rise and fall, early death and blockage tangle together—no one sorts them out.

sentences.zh: 仲任蔽其源，子長闡其惑。

translations.literal: Wang Chong obscured the source; Sima Qian clarified the confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong hid the root; Sima Qian opened the puzzle.

sentences.zh: 至於鶡冠甕牖，必以懸天有朞；

translations.literal: As for cap-and-window poverty, they insist there is a heaven-set term;
translations.idiomatic: The poor in cap and window insist heaven sets a term;

sentences.zh: 鼎貴高門，則曰唯人所召。

translations.literal: tripod-noble, high-gated families say only human summons.
translations.idiomatic: while tripod nobles in high gates say only men summon fortune.

sentences.zh: 譊譊讙咋，異端俱起。

translations.literal: Clamor and wrangling—heterodoxies rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Noise and quarrel—many heterodoxies arise at once.

sentences.zh: 蕭遠論其本而不暢其流，子玄語其流而未詳其本。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuanlun discussed the root but did not unfold the flow; Zi Xuan spoke the flow but did not detail the root.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuanlun treated the root but not the flow; Zi Xuan the flow but not the root.

sentences.zh: 嘗試言之曰：夫道生萬物，則謂之道；

translations.literal: I once tried to say: The Way begets the myriad things—this is called the Way;
translations.idiomatic: I once said: the Way begets all things—that is the Way;

sentences.zh: 生而無主，謂之自然。

translations.literal: living yet without a master, this is called the natural.
translations.idiomatic: life without a master is the natural.

sentences.zh: 自然者，物見其然，不知所以然；

translations.literal: The natural: things see that it is so, not why it is so;
translations.idiomatic: Natural means things see it is so, not why;

sentences.zh: 同焉皆得，不知所以得。

translations.literal: all alike attain, not knowing how they attain.
translations.idiomatic: all alike gain, not knowing how they gain.

sentences.zh: 鼓動陶鑄而不爲功，庶類混成而非其力；

translations.literal: It stirs and molds yet claims no merit; the myriad kinds blend into form yet not by its force;
translations.idiomatic: It stirs and molds without merit; myriad kinds form without its force;

sentences.zh: 生之無亭毒之心，死之豈虔劉之志；

translations.literal: in living it has no mind to nurture; in dying no will to slaughter;
translations.idiomatic: in life no mind to nurture; in death no will to slaughter;

sentences.zh: 墜之淵泉非其怒，昇之霄漢非其悅。

translations.literal: plunging into deep springs is not its anger, ascending the azure height not its pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: plunging into abyss is not anger, rising to heaven not pleasure.

sentences.zh: 蕩乎大乎，萬寶以之化；

translations.literal: Vast, great—the myriad treasures transform by it;
translations.idiomatic: Vast and great—myriad treasures transform by it;

sentences.zh: 確乎純乎，一作而不易。

translations.literal: firm, pure—one act and no change.
translations.idiomatic: firm and pure—one act, unchanging.

sentences.zh: 化而不易，則謂之命。

translations.literal: Transforming yet unchanging—this is called fate.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming yet unchanging—that is fate.

sentences.zh: 命也者，自天之命也。

translations.literal: Fate: what is mandated from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fate is what Heaven mandates.

sentences.zh: 定於冥兆，終然不變。

translations.literal: Fixed in dark omens, in the end unaltered.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in dark omens, finally unaltered.

sentences.zh: 鬼神莫能預，聖哲不能謀；

translations.literal: Ghosts and spirits cannot foretell, sages cannot plot;
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts cannot foretell, sages cannot plot;

sentences.zh: 觸山之力無以抗，倒日之誠弗能感；

translations.literal: strength to topple mountains cannot resist it, sincerity to overturn the sun cannot move it;
translations.idiomatic: strength to topple mountains cannot resist; sincerity to overturn the sun cannot move it;

sentences.zh: 短則不可緩之於寸陰，長則不可急之於箭漏；

translations.literal: the short cannot be stretched in a hair's breadth of shade, the long cannot be hurried by the drip of clepsydra;
translations.idiomatic: the short cannot be stretched in a moment, the long hurried by a water-clock drip;

sentences.zh: 至德未能逾，上智所不免。

translations.literal: utmost virtue cannot overstep it, highest wisdom cannot escape it.
translations.idiomatic: utmost virtue cannot overstep it, highest wisdom cannot escape it.

sentences.zh: 是以放勳之代，浩浩襄陵；

translations.literal: Hence in Yao's age floods piled to the hills;
translations.idiomatic: In Yao's age floods piled to the hills;

sentences.zh: 天乙之時，燋金流石。

translations.literal: in Tang's time metal scorched and stones flowed.
translations.idiomatic: in Tang's time metal scorched and stones ran like water.

sentences.zh: 文公𨆫其尾，宣尼絕其糧；

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin tugged his tail; Confucius ran out of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen tugged his tail; Confucius ran out of grain;

sentences.zh: 顏回敗其叢蘭，冉耕歌其芣苡；

translations.literal: Yan Hui's orchids withered; Ran Geng sang of plantain;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui's orchids withered; Ran Geng sang of plantain;

sentences.zh: 夷、叔斃淑媛之言，子輿困臧倉之訴。

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi died for a fair lady's words; Zengzi was trapped by Zang Cang's suit.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi died for a lady's words; Zengzi was trapped by Zang Cang's suit.

sentences.zh: 聖賢且猶若此，而況庸庸者乎！

translations.literal: Even sages were thus—how much more the mediocre!
translations.idiomatic: Even sages were thus—how much more ordinary men!

sentences.zh: 至乃伍員浮屍於江流，三閭沈骸於湘渚；

translations.literal: Down to Wu Zixu floating corpse on the river, Qu Yuan sinking bones in Xiang shallows;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu floated on the river, Qu Yuan sank in Xiang shallows;

sentences.zh: 賈大夫沮志於長沙，馮都尉皓發於郎署；

translations.literal: Jia Yi lost heart at Changsha, Feng Tang white-haired in the palace guard office;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi lost heart at Changsha, Feng Tang white-haired in the guard office;

sentences.zh: 君山鴻漸，鎩羽儀於高雲；

translations.literal: Jun Shan's wild goose flight, wings clipped in high clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Jun Shan's flight, wings clipped in high clouds;

sentences.zh: 敬通鳳起，摧迅翮於風穴：此豈才不足而行有遺哉？

translations.literal: Jing Tong's phoenix rise, swift pinions broken in the wind cave: was this insufficient talent or flawed conduct?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Tong's rise, pinions broken in the wind cave—lack of talent or flawed conduct?

sentences.zh: 近代有沛國劉瓛、瓛弟璡，並一時之秀士也。

translations.literal: In recent times Liu Huan of Pei and his younger brother Lin were both outstanding men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Liu Huan of Pei and his brother Lin were both outstanding men of the age.

sentences.zh: 瓛則關西孔子，通涉《六經》，循循善誘，服膺儒行。

translations.literal: Huan was Confucius of the west, versed in the Six Classics, gentle in teaching, devoted to Confucian conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was the west's Confucius, versed in the Six Classics, gentle in teaching, devoted to the rites.

sentences.zh: 璡則志烈秋霜，心貞昆玉，亭亭高竦，不雜風塵。

translations.literal: Lin's will was fierce as autumn frost, heart firm as Kun jade, towering high, unstained by dust.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's will was autumn frost, heart Kun jade, towering, unstained by dust.

sentences.zh: 皆毓德於衡門，並馳聲於天地。

translations.literal: Both nurtured virtue behind a humble gate and spread fame through heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Both nurtured virtue behind a humble gate and spread fame through heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 而官有微于侍郎，位不登於執戟，相繼徂落，宗祀無饗。

translations.literal: Yet office barely reached vice director and rank never attained halberd-bearer; they died in succession and the ancestral sacrifices went unfed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet office barely reached vice director and rank never halberd-bearer; they died in turn and sacrifices went unfed.

sentences.zh: 因斯兩賢，以言古則：昔之玉質金相，英髦秀達，皆擯斥於當年，韞奇才而莫用，候草木以共凋，與麋鹿而同死。

translations.literal: By these two worthies to speak of antiquity: jade quality and gold aspect, splendid talent—all were cast out in their day, talents hidden unused, waiting with grass and trees to wither, dying with deer.
translations.idiomatic: By these two: jade quality and gold aspect, splendid talent—all cast out in their day, talents unused, withering with grass and trees, dying with deer.

sentences.zh: 膏塗平原，骨填川谷，湮滅而無聞者，豈可勝道哉！

translations.literal: Grease smeared the plain, bones filled the valleys—those sunk and unheard, can they be counted!
translations.idiomatic: Grease on the plain, bones in the valleys—those sunk unheard, beyond counting!

sentences.zh: 此則宰衡之與皂隸，容、彭之與殤子，猗頓之與黔婁，陽文之與敦洽，咸得之於自然，不假道於才智。

translations.literal: Thus prime minister and clerk, Rong and Peng with the child who dies young, Yi Dun and Qian Lou, Yang Wen and Dun Xia—all from the natural, not by wit or ability.
translations.idiomatic: Prime minister and clerk, long life and early death, rich and poor—all from nature, not wit.

sentences.zh: 故曰「死生有命，富貴在天」，其斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: Hence "life and death have fate, wealth and honor are from Heaven"—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Hence "life and death have fate, wealth and honor from Heaven"—that is the sense.

sentences.zh: 然命體周流，變化非一，或先號後笑，或始吉終凶，或不召自來，或因人以濟。

translations.literal: Yet the body of fate circulates; change is not one—some wail first and laugh after, some auspicious at first and ill at end, some come unbidden, some succeed through others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fate circulates; change is not one—wail then laugh, auspicious then ill, come unbidden, succeed through others.

sentences.zh: 交錯紛糾，循環倚伏。

translations.literal: Crossed and tangled, cycling hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Crossed and tangled, cycling hidden and manifest.

sentences.zh: 非可以一理徵，非可以一途驗。

translations.literal: It cannot be verified by one principle nor tested on one path.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot be verified by one principle nor tested on one path.

sentences.zh: 而其道密微，寂寥忽慌，無形可以見，無聲可以聞。

translations.literal: Yet its way is secret and fine, lonely and dim—no form to see, no sound to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Its way is secret and fine, lonely and dim—no form to see, no sound to hear.

sentences.zh: 必御物以效靈，亦憑人而成象，譬天王之冕旒，任百官以司職。

translations.literal: It must ride things to show spirit and rely on men to form images—like the celestial king's cap-tassels, leaving the hundred officers each their charge.
translations.idiomatic: It rides things to show spirit and relies on men for images—like the king's cap, leaving officers their charge.

sentences.zh: 而惑者睹湯、武之龍躍，謂龕亂在神功；

translations.literal: Yet the deluded, seeing Tang and Wu's dragon leap, say pacifying chaos lay in divine merit;
translations.idiomatic: The deluded see Tang and Wu's dragon leap and say pacifying chaos was divine merit;

sentences.zh: 聞孔、墨之挺生，謂英睿擅奇響；

translations.literal: hearing Confucius and Mozi's birth, say keen brilliance monopolized rare fame;
translations.idiomatic: hear Confucius and Mozi born and say brilliance monopolized fame;

sentences.zh: 視彭、韓之豹變，謂鷙猛致人爵；

translations.literal: seeing Peng and Han's leopard change, say fierce valor won noble rank;
translations.idiomatic: see Peng and Han's leopard change and say fierceness won rank;

sentences.zh: 見張、桓之朱紱，謂明經拾青紫。

translations.literal: seeing Zhang and Huan's red cords, say mastering the classics picked purple and blue.
translations.idiomatic: see Zhang and Huan's red cords and say classics won purple rank.

sentences.zh: 豈知有力者運之而趨乎？

translations.literal: How would they know the powerful mover hurries it along?
translations.idiomatic: How would they know a powerful mover hurries it along?

sentences.zh: 故言而非命，有六蔽焉。

translations.literal: Thus to speak against fate there are six obscurations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus speaking against fate has six obscurations.

sentences.zh: 余請陳其梗概：

translations.literal: I ask leave to set forth the outline:
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to set forth the outline:

sentences.zh: 夫靡顏膩理，哆噅顣頞，形之異也；

translations.literal: Fine skin and greasy texture, gaping mouth and bulging cheeks—these are bodily differences;
translations.idiomatic: Fine skin, gaping mouth—these are bodily differences;

sentences.zh: 朝秀辰終，龜鶴千歲，年之殊也；

translations.literal: morning glory ends at dusk, tortoise and crane a thousand years—these are differences of years;
translations.idiomatic: morning glory ends at dusk, tortoise and crane a thousand years—differences of years;

sentences.zh: 聞言如響，智昏菽麥，神之辨也。

translations.literal: hearing words like echo, wit dim as beans and wheat—these are differences of spirit.
translations.idiomatic: hearing like echo, wit dim as beans—these are differences of spirit.

sentences.zh: 固知三者定乎造化，榮辱之境，獨曰由人。

translations.literal: So we know the three are fixed by creation, yet the realm of glory and shame they say comes from man alone.
translations.idiomatic: The three are fixed by creation, yet glory and shame they say come from man alone.

sentences.zh: 是知二五而未識於十，其蔽一也。

translations.literal: This is knowing two times five yet not ten—the first obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: This is knowing two fives but not ten—the first obscuration.

sentences.zh: 龍犀日角，帝王之表；

translations.literal: Dragon horn and sun brow—the emperor's form;
translations.idiomatic: Dragon horn and sun brow—the emperor's form;

sentences.zh: 河目龜文，公侯之相。

translations.literal: river eyes and tortoise pattern—the form of duke and marquis.
translations.idiomatic: river eyes and tortoise pattern—duke and marquis form.

sentences.zh: 撫鏡知其將刑，壓紐顯其膺錄。

translations.literal: stroking the mirror one knows coming execution; pressing the seal-knob shows the record of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: stroking the mirror one knows execution coming; pressing the seal-knob shows appointment.

sentences.zh: 星虹樞電，昭聖德之符；

translations.literal: star rainbow and pivot lightning manifest tokens of sage virtue;
translations.idiomatic: star rainbow and pivot lightning show sage virtue;

sentences.zh: 夜哭聚雲，鬱興王之瑞。

translations.literal: night weeping and cloud gathering are omens dense with a rising king.
translations.idiomatic: night weeping and cloud gathering are omens of a rising king.

sentences.zh: 皆兆發於前朞，渙汗於後葉。

translations.literal: All omens issue in an earlier term and pour forth in later generations.
translations.idiomatic: All omens issue in an earlier term and pour forth in later generations.

sentences.zh: 若謂驅貔虎，奮尺劍，入紫微，升帝道；

translations.literal: If one says driving tiger and leopard, wielding a foot-long sword, entering Purple Subtlety, ascending the imperial Way—
translations.idiomatic: If one says driving tiger and leopard, wielding a sword, entering Purple Subtlety, ascending the imperial Way—

sentences.zh: 則未達窅冥之情，未測神明之數，其蔽二也。

translations.literal: then one has not reached the feelings of the dark abyss nor measured the numbers of the divine—the second obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: then one has not reached the dark abyss nor measured divine numbers—the second obscuration.

sentences.zh: 空桑之里，變成洪川；

translations.literal: The village of Kongsang became a mighty river;
translations.idiomatic: The village of Kongsang became a mighty river;

sentences.zh: 歷陽之都，化爲魚鱉。

translations.literal: the capital of Liyang turned to fish and turtles.
translations.idiomatic: the capital of Liyang turned to fish and turtles.

sentences.zh: 楚師屠漢卒，睢河鯁其流；

translations.literal: Chu troops slaughtered Han soldiers; the Sui River choked on their corpses;
translations.idiomatic: Chu troops slaughtered Han soldiers; the Sui choked on corpses;

sentences.zh: 秦人坑趙士，沸聲若雷震。

translations.literal: Qin men buried Zhao soldiers; the boiling sound was like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Qin buried Zhao soldiers; the boiling sound was thunder.

sentences.zh: 火炎昆岳，礫石與琬琰俱焚；

translations.literal: Fire blazed on Kun peak; gravel and fine jade burned together;
translations.idiomatic: Fire on Kun peak; gravel and fine jade burned together;

sentences.zh: 嚴霜夜零，蕭艾與芝蘭共盡。

translations.literal: hard frost fell at night; wormwood and orchid perished together.
translations.idiomatic: hard frost at night; wormwood and orchid perished together.

sentences.zh: 雖游、夏之英才，伊、顏之殆庶，焉能抗之哉？

translations.literal: Though You and Xia were talented, Yi and Yan nearly sages—how could they resist?
translations.idiomatic: Though You and Xia were talented, Yi and Yan nearly sages—how resist?

sentences.zh: 其蔽三也。

translations.literal: The third obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: The third obscuration.

sentences.zh: 或曰，明月之珠，不能無纇；

translations.literal: Some say the bright-moon pearl cannot be without flaw;
translations.idiomatic: Some say the bright-moon pearl cannot be without flaw;

sentences.zh: 夏后之璜，不能無考。

translations.literal: the Xia sovereign's jade cannot be without crack.
translations.idiomatic: the Xia sovereign's jade cannot be without crack.

sentences.zh: 故亭伯死於縣長，長卿卒於園令，才非不傑也，主非不明也，而碎結綠之鴻輝，殘懸黎之夜色，抑尺之量有短哉？

translations.literal: Hence Ting Bo died under a county chief, Changqing died as park keeper—talent was not unheroic, rulers not unseeing, yet the splendor of joined green was shattered and dark jade's night hue marred—is the foot-rule sometimes short?
translations.idiomatic: Ting Bo died under a county chief, Sima Xiangru as park keeper—talent was not lacking, rulers not blind, yet splendor was shattered—is the measure sometimes short?

sentences.zh: 若然者，主父偃、公孫弘對策不升第，歷說而不入，牧豕淄原，見棄州部。

translations.literal: If so, Zhufu Yan and Gongsun Hong failed the policy exam, pleaded everywhere without entry, herded pigs on the Zi bank, abandoned by the province.
translations.idiomatic: If so, Zhufu Yan and Gongsun Hong failed the exam, pleaded without entry, herded pigs, abandoned by the province.

sentences.zh: 設令忽如過隙，溘死霜露，其爲詬恥，豈崔、馬之流乎？

translations.literal: Suppose they suddenly passed like a crack, died in frost and dew—would their shame match Cui and Ma?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose they passed like a crack and died in dew—would their shame match Cui and Ma?

sentences.zh: 及至開東閤，列五鼎，電照風行，聲馳海外，寧前愚而後智，先非而終是？

translations.literal: When they opened the eastern pavilion and set out five tripods, lightning flashed and wind ran, fame raced overseas—were they foolish before and wise after, wrong first and right in the end?
translations.idiomatic: When they opened the eastern pavilion and set five tripods, fame raced overseas—foolish before and wise after?

sentences.zh: 將榮悴有定數，天命有至極，而謬生妍蚩？

translations.literal: Or is glory and withering fixed in number, Heaven's mandate has an utmost limit, and we wrongly birth beauty and ugliness?
translations.idiomatic: Or is glory fixed in number and mandate has a limit, and we wrongly birth beauty and ugliness?

sentences.zh: 其蔽四也。

translations.literal: The fourth obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth obscuration.

sentences.zh: 夫虎嘯風馳，龍興雲屬，故重華立而元、凱升，辛受生而飛廉進。

translations.literal: Tiger roar, wind runs; dragon rises, clouds gather—thus when Chonghua stood, Yuan and Kai ascended; when Xin Shou was born, Fei Lian advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger roar, wind runs; dragon rises, clouds gather—Chonghua stood and Yuan and Kai rose; Xin Shou was born and Fei Lian advanced.

sentences.zh: 然則天下善人少，惡人多；

translations.literal: Thus under heaven good men are few, evil many;
translations.idiomatic: Thus good men are few, evil many;

sentences.zh: 闇主衆，明君寡。

translations.literal: dark lords many, bright lords few.
translations.idiomatic: dark lords many, bright lords few.

sentences.zh: 而薰蕕不同器，梟鸞不接翼。

translations.literal: Yet sweet grass and foul cannot share a vessel; owl and phoenix cannot wing together.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet grass and foul cannot share a vessel; owl and phoenix cannot wing together.

sentences.zh: 是使渾沌、檮杌，踵武雲臺之上；

translations.literal: This makes Hun Dun and Tao Wu tread Cloud Terrace's steps;
translations.idiomatic: This makes Hun Dun and Tao Wu tread Cloud Terrace;

sentences.zh: 仲容、庭堅，耕耘巖石之下。

translations.literal: Zhongrong and Ting Jian plow beneath the cliff rocks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong and Ting Jian plow beneath cliff rocks.

sentences.zh: 橫謂廢興在我，無繫於天，其蔽五也。

translations.literal: They insist rise and fall depend on me, not tied to Heaven—the fifth obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: They insist rise and fall depend on me, not Heaven—the fifth obscuration.

sentences.zh: 彼戎狄者，人面獸心，宴安鴆毒，以誅殺爲道德，以蒸報爲仁義。

translations.literal: Those Rong and Di: human face, beast heart, ease in poisoned wine, taking slaughter as morality and steaming revenge as benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Those barbarians: human face, beast heart, ease in poison, slaughter as morality, steaming revenge as benevolence.

sentences.zh: 雖大風立於青丘，鑿齒奮於華野，比其狼戾，曾何足逾。

translations.literal: Though the great wind stood at Green Hill and Zao Chi strove on Hua wild, compared with their savagery how could they be surpassed?
translations.idiomatic: Though the great wind stood at Green Hill and Zao Chi strove on Hua wild, compared with their savagery what surpasses them?

sentences.zh: 自金行不競，天地版蕩，左帶沸脣，乘間電發。

translations.literal: Since the Metal line could not compete, heaven and earth overturned, the left belt boiled with lip peoples, seizing the moment like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin line failed, heaven and earth overturned, border peoples boiled, seizing the moment like lightning.

sentences.zh: 遂覆瀍、洛，傾五都；

translations.literal: They overthrew Chan and Luo, toppled the five capitals;
translations.idiomatic: They overthrew Chan and Luo, toppled the five capitals;

sentences.zh: 居先王之桑梓，竊名號於中縣；

translations.literal: dwelt in the former kings' mulberry homeland, stole titles in the central counties;
translations.idiomatic: dwelt in the former kings' homeland, stole titles in the central counties;

sentences.zh: 與三皇競其氓黎，五帝角其區宇。

translations.literal: rivaled the Three Sovereigns for the people, contended with the Five Emperors for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: rivaled the Three Sovereigns for the people, contended with the Five Emperors for the realm.

sentences.zh: 種落繁熾，充牣神州。

translations.literal: Tribes multiplied and filled the divine land.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes multiplied and filled the divine land.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 福善禍淫，徒虛言耳。

translations.literal: Bless the good and punish the evil—empty words only.
translations.idiomatic: Bless the good and punish the evil—empty words only.

sentences.zh: 豈非否泰相傾，盈縮遞運，而汩之以人？

translations.literal: Is it not decline and peace leaning on each other, full and empty turning in turn, yet muddied by attributing it to man?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not decline and peace leaning, full and empty turning, yet muddied by man?

sentences.zh: 其蔽六也。

translations.literal: The sixth obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth obscuration.

sentences.zh: 然所謂命者，死生焉，貴賤焉，貧富焉，理亂焉，禍福焉，此十者天之所賦也。

translations.literal: What is called fate: life and death, noble and base, poor and rich, order and chaos, fortune and disaster—these ten Heaven bestows.
translations.idiomatic: Fate: life and death, noble and base, poor and rich, order and chaos, fortune and disaster—ten things Heaven bestows.

sentences.zh: 愚智善惡，此四者人之所行也。

translations.literal: Foolish and wise, good and evil—these four man performs.
translations.idiomatic: Foolish and wise, good and evil—these four man performs.

sentences.zh: 夫神非舜、禹，心異朱、均，才絓中庸，在於所習。

translations.literal: Spirit is not Yao and Shun's alone; hearts differ like Zhu and Jun; talent snags on the mean—its place is in what is practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit is not Yao and Shun's alone; hearts differ; talent snags on the mean—in practice.

sentences.zh: 是以素絲無恒，玄黃代起；

translations.literal: Hence plain silk has no constancy; black and yellow rise in turn;
translations.idiomatic: Plain silk has no constancy; black and yellow rise in turn;

sentences.zh: 鮑魚芳蘭，入而自變。

translations.literal: saltfish and orchid—enter and change of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: saltfish and orchid—enter and change of themselves.

sentences.zh: 故季路學於仲尼，厲風霜之節；

translations.literal: Thus Zilu studied with Zhongni and forged frost-and-wind integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Zilu studied with Confucius and forged frost-and-wind integrity;

sentences.zh: 楚穆謀於潘崇，成悖逆之禍。

translations.literal: Chu Mu plotted with Pan Chong and achieved rebellious disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Mu plotted with Pan Chong and achieved rebellious disaster.

sentences.zh: 而商臣之惡，盛業光於後嗣；

translations.literal: yet Shang Chen's evil let his great enterprise shine on later heirs;
translations.idiomatic: yet Shang Chen's evil let his enterprise shine on heirs;

sentences.zh: 仲由之善，不能息其結纓。

translations.literal: Zhong You's good could not cancel his knotted cap at death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You's good could not cancel his knotted cap at death.

sentences.zh: 斯則邪正由於人，吉凶存乎命。

translations.literal: Thus crooked and straight come from man; fortune and ill rest in fate.
translations.idiomatic: Crooked and straight come from man; fortune and ill rest in fate.

sentences.zh: 或以鬼神害盈，皇天輔德。

translations.literal: Some say ghosts and spirits harm the full and August Heaven aids virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Some say spirits harm the full and Heaven aids virtue.

sentences.zh: 故宋公一言，法星三徙；

translations.literal: Hence Duke Song's one word moved the law star thrice;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Song's one word moved the law star thrice;

sentences.zh: 殷帝自翦，千里來雲。

translations.literal: the Yin emperor cut himself and clouds came a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: the Yin emperor cut himself and clouds came a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 善惡無徵，未洽斯義。

translations.literal: Good and evil without tokens—this meaning is not yet reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil without tokens—this is not yet reconciled.

sentences.zh: 且于公高門以待封，嚴母掃墓以望喪。

translations.literal: Moreover Duke Yu's high gate awaited enfeoffment; Yan's mother swept the tomb awaiting mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yu's high gate awaited enfeoffment; Yan's mother swept the tomb awaiting mourning.

sentences.zh: 此君子所以自強不息也。

translations.literal: This is why the gentleman strengthens himself unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the gentleman strengthens himself unceasingly.

sentences.zh: 如使仁而無報，奚爲修善立名乎？

translations.literal: If benevolence had no reward, why cultivate goodness and establish a name?
translations.idiomatic: If benevolence had no reward, why cultivate goodness and establish a name?

sentences.zh: 斯徑廷之辭也。

translations.literal: This is courtyard-wide talk.
translations.idiomatic: This is courtyard-wide talk.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人之言，顯而晦，微而婉，幽遠而難聞，河漢而不極。

translations.literal: The sage's words are manifest yet obscure, subtle yet mild, far and hard to hear, like the Milky Way without end.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's words are manifest yet obscure, far and hard to hear, like the Milky Way without end.

sentences.zh: 或立教以進庸惰，或言命以窮性靈。

translations.literal: Sometimes he sets up teaching to advance the dull and lazy, sometimes speaks fate to exhaust the spiritual nature.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he teaches to advance the dull; sometimes speaks fate to exhaust the spirit.

sentences.zh: 積善餘慶，立教也；

translations.literal: "Heaping good leaves surplus blessing"—that is teaching;
translations.idiomatic: "Heaping good leaves surplus blessing"—that is teaching;

sentences.zh: 鳳鳥不至，言命也。

translations.literal: "The phoenix bird does not come"—that is speaking fate.
translations.idiomatic: "The phoenix does not come"—that is speaking fate.

sentences.zh: 今以其片言辯其要趨，何異乎夕死之類而論春秋之變哉？

translations.literal: Now to argue its gist from a fragment—how is it unlike those who die at dusk yet discuss the Spring and Autumn changes?
translations.idiomatic: To argue the gist from a fragment—how unlike dying at dusk yet discussing Spring and Autumn changes?

sentences.zh: 且荊昭德音，丹雲不卷；

translations.literal: Moreover King Zhao of Chu's virtuous sound did not roll up cinnabar clouds;
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Chu's virtuous sound did not roll cinnabar clouds;

sentences.zh: 周宣祈雨，珪璧斯罄。

translations.literal: King Xuan of Zhou prayed for rain and jade scepters were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan of Zhou prayed for rain and jade scepters were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 于叟種德，不逮勳、華之高；

translations.literal: Old Yu planted virtue yet did not reach the height of Xun and Hua;
translations.idiomatic: Old Yu planted virtue yet did not reach Xun and Hua;

sentences.zh: 延年殘獷，未甚東陵之酷。

translations.literal: Yan Nian was cruel and fierce yet not as bad as Dongling's bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Nian was cruel yet not as bad as Dongling.

sentences.zh: 爲善一，爲惡均，而禍福異其流，廢興殊其迹。

translations.literal: doing one good, one evil equal, yet fortune and disaster differ in their streams, rise and fall differ in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: one good, one evil equal, yet fortune and disaster differ, rise and fall differ.

sentences.zh: 蕩蕩上帝，豈如是乎？

translations.literal: Vast August Heaven—could it be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Vast Heaven—could it be like this?

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「風雨如晦，雞鳴不已。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Wind and rain like night, the cock crows unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Wind and rain like night, the cock crows unceasingly.

sentences.zh: 」故善人爲善，焉有息哉？

translations.literal: " Thus the good man doing good—how could he rest?
translations.idiomatic: Thus the good man doing good—how could he rest?

sentences.zh: 夫食稻梁，進芻豢，衣狐貉，襲冰紈，觀窈眇之奇儛，聽雲和之琴瑟，此生人之所急，非有求而爲也。

translations.literal: To eat millet and rice, advance fodder and fatlings, wear fox and badger, don ice-white silk, watch subtle wonders dance, hear Yunhe lutes and zithers—this living men urgently desire, not because they sought it.
translations.idiomatic: To eat grain and meat, wear fur and silk, watch subtle dances, hear Yunhe music—living men desire this, not from seeking.

sentences.zh: 修道德，習仁義，敦孝悌，立忠貞，漸禮樂之腴潤，蹈先王之盛則，此君子之所急，非有求而爲也。

translations.literal: To cultivate the Way and virtue, practice benevolence and righteousness, thicken filial piety and brotherhood, establish loyalty and steadfastness, steep in the rich moisture of rites and music, tread the former kings' great pattern—this the gentleman urgently desires, not because he sought it.
translations.idiomatic: To cultivate the Way, practice benevolence, thicken filial piety, establish loyalty, steep in rites and music, tread the former kings' pattern—the gentleman desires this, not from seeking.

sentences.zh: 然而君子居正體道，樂天知命。

translations.literal: Yet the gentleman dwells in rectitude and embodies the Way, delights in Heaven and knows fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gentleman dwells in rectitude and embodies the Way, delights in Heaven and knows fate.

sentences.zh: 明其無可奈何，識其不由智力。

translations.literal: He clarifies what cannot be helped and knows it does not come from intellect and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He clarifies what cannot be helped and knows it does not come from intellect and strength.

sentences.zh: 逝而不召，來而不距，生而不喜，死而不戚。

translations.literal: What departs he does not summon; what comes he does not reject; living he is not glad; dying he is not grieved.
translations.idiomatic: What departs he does not summon; what comes he does not reject; living not glad; dying not grieved.

sentences.zh: 瑤臺夏屋，不能悅其神；

translations.literal: Jade terraces and summer halls cannot gladden his spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Jade terraces and summer halls cannot gladden his spirit;

sentences.zh: 土室編蓬，未足憂其慮。

translations.literal: earthen rooms and woven rush are not enough to trouble his cares.
translations.idiomatic: earthen rooms and woven rush are not enough to trouble his cares.

sentences.zh: 不充詘於富貴，不遑遑於所欲。

translations.literal: He does not puff up in wealth and honor, does not hurry after desires.
translations.idiomatic: He does not puff up in wealth and honor, does not hurry after desires.

sentences.zh: 豈有史公、董相《不遇》之文乎？

translations.literal: Would he have the Unappreciated essays of Lord Shi and Chancellor Dong?
translations.idiomatic: Would he write Unappreciated essays like Sima Qian and Dong Zhongshu?

sentences.zh: 論成，中山劉沼致書以難之，凡再反，峻並爲申析以答之。

translations.literal: When the discourse was finished Liu Zhao of Zhongshan sent a letter to challenge it; twice he replied and Jun answered each with analysis.
translations.idiomatic: When the discourse was done Liu Zhao of Zhongshan challenged it; twice he replied and Jun answered with analysis.

sentences.zh: 會沼卒，不見峻後報者，峻乃爲書以序之曰：「劉侯旣有斯難，值余有天倫之戚，竟未之致也。

translations.literal: When Zhao died Jun never saw the later reply; Jun then wrote a preface saying: "Lord Liu had this challenge, but I had domestic grief and never delivered my answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao died Jun never saw the later reply; he wrote a preface: "Lord Liu had this challenge, but I had domestic grief and never answered.

sentences.zh: 尋而此君長逝，化爲異物，緒言餘論，蘊而莫傳。

translations.literal: Soon this gentleman passed away and became another thing; his threads of argument lay hidden and were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he passed away; his arguments lay hidden and were not transmitted.

sentences.zh: 或有自其家得而示余者，悲其音徽未沫，而其人已亡，青簡尚新，而宿草將列，泫然不知涕之無從。

translations.literal: Someone obtained them from his house and showed me; I grieved that his tone was not yet faded while the man was gone, the green bamboo still fresh while grave grass would soon be ranked—tears fell and I did not know whence they came.
translations.idiomatic: Someone showed me his papers; I grieved his tone not faded while the man was gone, bamboo fresh while grave grass would soon rise—tears fell unawares.

sentences.zh: 雖隙駟不留，尺波電謝；

translations.literal: Though the gap-team does not stay, the foot of wave flashes like lightning;
translations.idiomatic: Though the gap-team does not stay, the wave flashes like lightning;

sentences.zh: 而秋菊春蘭，英華靡絕。

translations.literal: autumn chrysanthemum and spring orchid—splendor never ends.
translations.idiomatic: autumn chrysanthemum and spring orchid—splendor never ends.

sentences.zh: 故存其梗概，更酬其旨。

translations.literal: Therefore I keep the outline and answer his intent again.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I keep the outline and answer his intent again.

sentences.zh: 若使墨翟之言無爽，宣室之談有徵。

translations.literal: If Mozi's words were not in error and the Xuan chamber talk had proof—
translations.idiomatic: If Mozi's words were not wrong and the Xuan chamber talk had proof—

sentences.zh: 冀東平之樹，望咸陽而西靡；

translations.literal: I would hope the tree at Dongping, gazing at Xianyang, bends west;
translations.idiomatic: I would hope the tree at Dongping, gazing at Xianyang, bends west;

sentences.zh: 蓋山之泉，聞弦歌而赴節。

translations.literal: the spring on Gai Mountain, hearing string songs, matches the beat.
translations.idiomatic: the spring on Gai Mountain, hearing string songs, matches the beat.

sentences.zh: 但懸劍空壟，有恨如何！

translations.literal: But the sword hangs over an empty mound—what regret can match!
translations.idiomatic: But the sword hangs over an empty mound—what regret can match!

sentences.zh: 」其論文多不載。

translations.literal: " Most of the discourse is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the discourse is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 峻又嘗爲《自序》，其略曰：「余自比馮敬通，而有同之者三，異之者四。

translations.literal: Jun also once wrote a Self-Preface, in brief: "I compare myself to Feng Jingtong with three likenesses and four differences.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also wrote a Self-Preface: "I compare myself to Feng Jingtong with three likenesses and four differences.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 敬通雄才冠世，志剛金石；

translations.literal: Jingtong's heroic talent topped the age, his will firm as metal and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong's talent topped the age, his will firm as metal and stone;

sentences.zh: 余雖不及之，而節亮慷慨，此一同也。

translations.literal: I do not reach him, yet in integrity and generous spirit this is one likeness.
translations.idiomatic: I do not reach him, yet in integrity and generous spirit—one likeness.

sentences.zh: 敬通值中興明君，而終不試用；

translations.literal: Jingtong met a bright lord at restoration yet in the end was not tried;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong met a bright lord at restoration yet was never tried;

sentences.zh: 余逢命世英主，亦擯斥當年，此二同也。

translations.literal: I met a fate-shaping brilliant lord yet was also cast out in my year—this is the second likeness.
translations.idiomatic: I met a brilliant lord yet was cast out in my year—the second likeness.

sentences.zh: 敬通有忌妻，至於身操井臼；

translations.literal: Jingtong had a jealous wife, to the point of working the well and mortar himself;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong had a jealous wife, to the point of working the well and mortar himself;

sentences.zh: 余有悍室，亦令家道晳感軻，此三同也。

translations.literal: I have a fierce wife who also cramped the household as in the tale of the narrow rut—this is the third likeness.
translations.idiomatic: I have a fierce wife who also cramped the household like the narrow rut—the third likeness.

sentences.zh: 敬通當更始之世，手握兵符，躍馬食肉；

translations.literal: Jingtong in Gengshi's age held the tally and leapt on horse to eat meat;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong in Gengshi's age held the tally and leapt on horse to eat meat;

sentences.zh: 余自少迄長，戚戚無歡，此一異也。

translations.literal: from youth to age I have been sorrowful without joy—this is the first difference.
translations.idiomatic: from youth to age I have been sorrowful without joy—the first difference.

sentences.zh: 敬通有一子仲文，官成名立；

translations.literal: Jingtong had a son Zhongwen who achieved office and fame;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong had a son Zhongwen who achieved office and fame;

sentences.zh: 余禍同伯道，永無血胤，此二異也。

translations.literal: my misfortune matches Bo Dao—I shall never have blood heirs—this is the second difference.
translations.idiomatic: my misfortune matches Bo Dao—I shall never have heirs—the second difference.

sentences.zh: 敬通膂力方剛，老而益壯；

translations.literal: Jingtong's sinew and strength were just firm and in old age grew stronger;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong's strength was just firm and in old age grew stronger;

sentences.zh: 余有犬馬之疾，溘死無時，此三異也。

translations.literal: I have dog-and-horse illness and may die at any time—this is the third difference.
translations.idiomatic: I have chronic illness and may die at any time—the third difference.

sentences.zh: 敬通雖芝殘蕙焚，終填溝壑，而爲名賢所慕，其風流郁烈芬芳，久而彌盛；

translations.literal: Jingtong though orchid and iris were burned still filled the ditch, yet famous worthies admired him; his wind and fragrance were dense and long grew stronger;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong though orchid and iris burned still filled the ditch, yet worthies admired him; his fragrance long grew stronger;

sentences.zh: 余聲塵寂漠，世不吾知，魂魄一去，將同秋草，此四異也。

translations.literal: my name and dust are silent, the age does not know me; once soul departs I shall be autumn grass—this is the fourth difference.
translations.idiomatic: my name is silent, the age does not know me; once soul departs I am autumn grass—the fourth difference.

sentences.zh: 所以自力爲敘，遺之好事云。

translations.literal: Therefore I force myself to write this account and leave it for lovers of such things."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I force myself to write this and leave it for lovers of such things."

sentences.zh: 」峻居東陽，吳、會人士多從其學。

translations.literal: Jun dwelt in Dongyang; many men of Wu and Kuai came to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun dwelt in Dongyang; many men of Wu and Kuai studied with him.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year two he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 門人諡曰玄靖先生。

translations.literal: His disciples gave the posthumous title Master Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples gave the posthumous title Master Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 劉沼字明信，中山魏昌人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao, courtesy name Mingxin, was a man of Weichang in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao, styled Mingxin, came from Weichang in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 六代祖輿，晉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yu was Jin General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Yu was Jin general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 沼幼善屬文，旣長博學。

translations.literal: Zhao in youth was skilled at composition; when grown he was broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhao wrote well; grown, he was widely learned.

sentences.zh: 仕齊起家奉朝請，冠軍行參軍。

translations.literal: In Qi he first took office as Court Attendant and Champion acting aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he began as court attendant and champion acting aide.

sentences.zh: 天監初，拜後軍臨川王記室參軍，秣陵令，卒。

translations.literal: Early Tianjian he was made Rear Army Prince of Linchuan staff secretary and Moling magistrate, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he served Linchuan prince as staff secretary and governed Moling, then died.

sentences.zh: 謝幾卿，陳郡陽夏人。

translations.literal: Xie Jiqing was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jiqing was from Yangxia in Chen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖靈運，宋臨川內史；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Lingyun was Song Administrator of Linchuan;
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Lingyun was Song Linchuan administrator;

sentences.zh: 父超宗，齊黃門郎；

translations.literal: his father Chaozong was Qi Gentleman of the Yellow Gate;
translations.idiomatic: father Chaozong was Qi yellow-gate gentleman;

sentences.zh: 並有重名於前代。

translations.literal: both had great fame in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: both were famed in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 幾卿幼清辯，當世號曰神童。

translations.literal: Jiqing in youth was clear in debate; his age called him a wonder-child.
translations.idiomatic: Young Jiqing debated clearly; his age called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 後超宗坐事徙越州，路出新亭渚，幾卿不忍辭訣，遂投赴江流，左右馳救，得不沉溺。

translations.literal: Later when Chaozong was banished to Yuezhou and passed Xinting ford, Jiqing could not bear parting and threw himself into the river; attendants raced to save him and he did not drown.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaozong was exiled to Yue and passed Xinting, Jiqing leapt into the river; aides saved him from drowning.

sentences.zh: 及居父憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: In his father's mourning his grief exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his father, he grieved beyond the rites.

sentences.zh: 服闋，召補國子生。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as National University student.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he entered the National University.

sentences.zh: 齊文惠太子自臨策試，謂祭酒王儉曰：「幾卿本長玄理，今可以經義訪之。

translations.literal: Qi Crown Prince Wen Hui personally presided at the examination and told Libationer Wang Jian: "Jiqing has long excelled in dark learning; now you may question him on the meaning of the classics."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui prince tested him himself and told Wang Jian: "Jiqing masters dark learning; examine him on the classics."

sentences.zh: 」儉承旨發問，幾卿隨事辨對，辭無滯者，文惠大稱賞焉。

translations.literal: Jian followed the intent and questioned him; Jiqing answered every point without hesitation, and Wen Hui greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian questioned him; Jiqing answered without pause and Wen Hui praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 儉謂人曰：「謝超宗爲不死矣。」

translations.literal: Jian told others: "Xie Chaozong is not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said: "Xie Chaozong lives again."

sentences.zh: 旣長好學，博涉有文采。

translations.literal: Grown, he loved learning, was broadly versed, and had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he studied widely and wrote with grace.

sentences.zh: 起家豫章王國常侍，累遷車騎法曹行參軍、相國祭酒。

translations.literal: He began as Regular Attendant of the Prince of Yuzhang, rising to Cavalry General law-court acting aide and prince libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He began in Yuzhang prince's service, rose to cavalry law aide and prince libationer.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧國令，入補尚書殿中郎、太尉晉安王主簿。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Ningguo, returned as Secretariat palace gentleman and Grand Marshal Prince of Jin'an chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Ningguo, then became secretariat palace gentleman and Jin'an prince chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除征虜鄱陽王記室、尚書三公侍郎，尋爲治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Early Tianjian he was made staff secretary to the Pacification Army Prince of Poyang and Secretariat third-rank gentleman, soon Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was Poyang staff secretary and secretariat gentleman, soon imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 舊郎官轉爲此職者，世謂爲南奔。

translations.literal: Former custom called transfer from gentleman to this post "running south."
translations.idiomatic: Office gentlemen called this transfer "fleeing south."

sentences.zh: 幾卿頗失志，多陳疾，臺事略不復理。

translations.literal: Jiqing was much disappointed, often pleaded illness, and basically ignored Board business.
translations.idiomatic: Dispirited, he often feigned illness and neglected ministry work.

sentences.zh: 徙爲散騎侍郎，累遷中書郎、國子博士、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to Supernumerary Cavalry Gentleman, rising to Secretariat gentleman, National University erudite, and Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became supernumerary cavalry gentleman, then secretariat gentleman, university erudite, and secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 幾卿詳悉故實，僕射徐勉每有疑滯，多詢訪之。

translations.literal: Jiqing knew past matters in detail; Vice Director Xu Mian whenever doubtful would consult him.
translations.idiomatic: He knew antiquities; Xu Mian often asked his advice.

sentences.zh: 然性通脫，會意便行，不拘朝憲。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was free and easy; where intent struck he acted, not bound by court statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was free-spirited and ignored court decorum when mood moved him.

sentences.zh: 嘗預樂游苑宴，不得醉而還，因詣道邊酒壚，停車褰幔，與車前三騶對飲，時觀者如堵，幾卿處之自若。

translations.literal: Once at a Leyou Park feast he returned without getting drunk and stopped at a roadside wine shop, lifted the curtain of his carriage, and drank facing the three outriders before his coach; onlookers packed like a wall yet Jiqing was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Drunkless after Leyou feast, he drank with his outriders at a roadside inn while crowds stared unabashed.

sentences.zh: 後以在省署，夜著犢鼻褌，與門生登閣道飲酒酣嘑，爲有司糾奏，坐免官。

translations.literal: Later in the provincial office he wore crotchless shorts at night and caroused with students on the gallery, shouting drunk; the authorities impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Caught drinking on the gallery in shorts at night, he was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋起爲國子博士，俄除河東太守，秩未滿，陳疾解。

translations.literal: Soon reappointed National University erudite, soon Hedong Administrator; before his term ended he pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon erudite again, then Hedong governor; he resigned ill before term's end.

sentences.zh: 尋除太子率更令，遷鎮衛南平王長史。

translations.literal: Soon Crown Prince Rate Officer, then Chief Secretary to the Pacification Guard Prince of Pingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon crown prince rate officer, then Pingnan prince chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 普通六年，詔遣領軍將軍西昌侯蕭淵藻督衆軍北伐，幾卿啓求行，擢爲軍師長史，加威戎將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong an edict sent General Who Pacifies the Army Marquis of Xichang Xiao Yuanyu to lead armies north; Jiqing asked to go and was promoted to Chief Secretary and Weirong General.
translations.idiomatic: Putong year six he joined Marquis of Xichang Xiao Yuanyu's northern campaign as chief secretary and weirong general.

sentences.zh: 軍至渦陽退敗，幾卿坐免官。

translations.literal: When the army retreated defeated at Woyang, Jiqing was dismissed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat at Woyang cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 居宅在白楊石井，朝中交好者載酒從之，賓客滿坐。

translations.literal: His home was at White Poplar Stone Well; court friends brought wine to him and guests filled the seats.
translations.idiomatic: At White Poplar Stone Well court friends flocked with wine.

sentences.zh: 時左丞庾仲容亦免歸，二人意志相得，並肆情誕縱，或乘露車歷遊郊野，旣醉則執鐸輓歌，不屑物議。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yu Zhongrong was also dismissed and returned; the two wills matched and they indulged wildly together, sometimes riding open carriages through suburbs; drunk they would take bells and sing, heedless of public talk.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed Yu Zhongrong joined him in wild outings, singing with bells and scorning opinion.

sentences.zh: 湘東王在荊鎮，與書慰勉之。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong at his Jing post wrote to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong in Jingzhou wrote to console him.

sentences.zh: 幾卿答曰：「下官自奉違南浦，卷迹東郊，望日臨風，瞻言佇立。

translations.literal: Jiqing replied: "Your humble servant since parting from the southern ford has withdrawn tracks to the eastern suburbs; day by day facing the wind, I stand gazing in speech."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Since leaving the southern ford I hide in the eastern suburbs, daily facing the wind in longing."

sentences.zh: 仰尋惠渥，陪奉遊宴，漾桂棹於清池，席落英於曾岨。

translations.literal: Looking up I recall your kindness, accompanying your tours and feasts, floating cassia oars on clear pools and spreading fallen blossoms on layered hills.
translations.idiomatic: I recall your kindness at feasts—cassia boats on clear pools, blossoms on layered hills.

sentences.zh: 蘭香兼御，羽觴競集，側聽餘論，沐浴玄流。

translations.literal: Orchid fragrance on both sides, feathered cups competing; listening to the overflow of discourse I bathed in dark learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid scent and competing cups; I heard your discourse and bathed in dark learning.

sentences.zh: 濤波之辯，懸河不足譬；

translations.literal: Debate like surging waves—hanging rivers are not enough to compare;
translations.idiomatic: Debate like surging waves outdid hanging rivers;

sentences.zh: 春藻之辭，麗文無以匹。

translations.literal: spring foliage in phrasing—ornate text has no match.
translations.idiomatic: spring foliage in phrasing had no match.

sentences.zh: 莫不相顧動容，服心勝口，不覺春日爲遙，更謂脩夜爲促。

translations.literal: All turned to look moved, convinced in heart beyond words, not noticing spring days as distant or long nights as short.
translations.idiomatic: All were moved, convinced beyond words, not feeling spring distant or night short.

sentences.zh: 嘉會難常，摶雲易遠，言念如昨，忽焉素秋。

translations.literal: Fine meetings are hard to keep; clutching clouds is easily far—thinking of yesterday, suddenly it is plain autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Fine meetings fade; yesterday feels suddenly like autumn.

sentences.zh: 恩光不遺，善謔遠降。

translations.literal: Your grace does not abandon me; kind jest descends from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace remains; kind words come from afar.

sentences.zh: 因事罷歸，豈雲棲息。

translations.literal: Dismissed on business and returned—is that called resting?
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed on business—is that rest?

sentences.zh: 旣匪高官，理就一廛。

translations.literal: I am not a high official; reason leads to one hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: No high office—only one hamlet suits me.

sentences.zh: 田家作苦，實符清誨。

translations.literal: Farm work is bitter; it truly fits your pure teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Farm toil is bitter, as your teaching says.

sentences.zh: 本乏金羈之飾，無假玉璧爲資；

translations.literal: Originally I lacked gold bridle ornaments and had no jade disks for capital;
translations.idiomatic: I lacked gold trappings and jade capital;

sentences.zh: 徒以老使形疏，疾令心阻，沉滯床簟，彌歷七旬。

translations.literal: only age makes the form sparse and illness blocks the heart, sunk on the couch more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: age thins me and illness blocks the heart—seventy days on the couch.

sentences.zh: 夢幻俄頃，憂傷在念，竟知無益，思自袪遣。

translations.literal: Dreams and illusion in a moment; sorrow in mind knows it is useless and I think to cast it off.
translations.idiomatic: Dreams pass in a moment; sorrow is useless and I would cast it off.

sentences.zh: 尋理滌意，即以任命爲膏酥；

translations.literal: Seeking principle to cleanse intent, I take appointment as salve;
translations.idiomatic: Seeking clarity, I take office as salve;

sentences.zh: 攬鏡照形，翻以支離代萱樹。

translations.literal: holding the mirror to see form, I instead take deformity for the daylily tree.
translations.idiomatic: in the mirror I see deformity where others see daylilies.

sentences.zh: 故得仰慕徽猷，永言前哲；

translations.literal: Thus I look up to lofty tracks and forever speak of sages past;
translations.idiomatic: So I honor sages past;

sentences.zh: 鬼穀深棲，接輿高舉；

translations.literal: Gui Guzi dwelt deep; Jie Yu held high;
translations.idiomatic: Gui Guzi hid deep; Jie Yu held high;

sentences.zh: 遁名屠肆，發迹關市；

translations.literal: hid their names in butcher stalls, rose from barrier markets;
translations.idiomatic: names in butcher stalls, rise from market gates;

sentences.zh: 其人緬邈，餘流可想。

translations.literal: those men are remote; their traces may be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: those men are far; their traces remain.

sentences.zh: 若令亡者有知，寧不縈悲玄壤，悵隔芳塵；

translations.literal: If the dead have awareness, would they not grieve in dark earth, bitter at separation from fragrant dust;
translations.idiomatic: If the dead know, they grieve in dark earth, parted from life;

sentences.zh: 如其逝者可作，必當昭被光景，歡同遊豫；

translations.literal: if the departed could act, they would surely shine in light and joy as in former tours;
translations.idiomatic: if the dead could act, they would shine as in former tours;

sentences.zh: 使夫一介老圃，得簉虛心末席。

translations.literal: let this one old gardener join the empty seat at the end.
translations.idiomatic: let this old gardener join the last seat.

sentences.zh: 去日已疏，來侍未孱；

translations.literal: The day of parting is already sparse; coming attendance is not yet weak;
translations.idiomatic: Parting is long past; new attendance is not slight;

sentences.zh: 連劍飛鳧，擬非其類；

translations.literal: linked swords and flying ducks are not my kind;
translations.idiomatic: linked swords and flying ducks are not my kind;

sentences.zh: 懷私茂德，竊用涕零。」

translations.literal: cherishing private virtue I steal tears."
translations.idiomatic: cherishing your virtue I weep in private."

sentences.zh: 幾卿雖不持檢操，然於家門篤睦。

translations.literal: Though Jiqing did not restrain conduct, in the family he was deeply affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: Though unrestrained, he was deeply affectionate at home.

sentences.zh: 兄才卿早卒，其子藻幼孤，幾卿撫養甚至。

translations.literal: Elder brother Caicheng died early; his son Zao was young and orphaned; Jiqing raised him with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Caicheng died young; Jiqing raised orphan Zao devotedly.

sentences.zh: 及藻成立，歷清官公府祭酒、主簿，皆幾卿獎訓之力也。

translations.literal: When Zao was established, his clear offices as household libationer and chief clerk were all through Jiqing's encouragement and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's offices came from Jiqing's training.

sentences.zh: 世以此稱之。

translations.literal: The age praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The age praised it.

sentences.zh: 幾卿未及序用，病卒。

translations.literal: Jiqing before he could be employed in order died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died ill before full use.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works circulated.

sentences.zh: 劉勰字彥和，東莞莒人。

translations.literal: Liu Xie, styled Yanhe, was a man of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xie, styled Yanhe, was from Ju in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 祖靈真，宋司空秀之弟也。

translations.literal: Grandfather Lingzhen was younger brother of Song Minister of Works Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Lingzhen was younger brother of Song Minister of Works Xiu.

sentences.zh: 父尚，越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Father Shang was Rapid Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Father Shang was rapid cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 勰早孤，篤志好學。

translations.literal: Xie was orphaned early, devoted in will and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he studied devotedly.

sentences.zh: 家貧不婚娶，依沙門僧祐，與之居處，積十餘年，遂博通經論，因區別部類，錄而序之。

translations.literal: The family was poor and he did not marry; he relied on the monk Sengyou, living with him more than ten years, until he thoroughly mastered sutras and treatises and sorted them by category, recording and ordering them.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and unmarried, he lived with monk Sengyou ten years, mastered sutras, and classified the canon.

sentences.zh: 今定林寺經藏，勰所定也。

translations.literal: The scripture treasury of Dinglin Temple today was fixed by Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Dinglin Temple's canon was his ordering.

sentences.zh: 天監初，起家奉朝請、中軍臨川王宏引兼記室，遷車騎倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Early Tianjian he began as Court Attendant; Prince of Linchuan Hong of the Center Army summoned him as acting staff secretary, then Cavalry storehouse acting aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was court attendant, then Linchuan prince staff secretary and cavalry storehouse aide.

sentences.zh: 出爲太末令，政有清績。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Taimo; his administration had pure achievement.
translations.idiomatic: As Taimo magistrate his rule was exemplary.

sentences.zh: 除仁威南康王記室，兼東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was made staff secretary to Benevolent Might Prince of Nankang and Eastern Palace Communications Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nankang staff secretary and Eastern Palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時七廟饗薦已用蔬果，而二郊農社猶有犧牲。

translations.literal: At that time the seven temples' offerings already used fruits and vegetables, but the two suburban altars and agricultural and community rites still had victims.
translations.idiomatic: Seven temples used fruit; two suburbs still sacrificed animals.

sentences.zh: 勰乃表言二郊宜與七廟同改，詔付尚書議，依勰所陳。

translations.literal: Xie memorialized that the two suburbs should be changed like the seven temples; an edict sent it to the Ministry of Rites to discuss, and they followed what Xie stated.
translations.idiomatic: He urged matching suburbs to temples; the ministry agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉，兼舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Infantry Commandant, still Communications Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to infantry commandant while keeping attendant duty.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子好文學，深愛接之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming loved literature and deeply favored and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming prince loved letters and favored him.

sentences.zh: 初，勰撰《文心雕龍》五十篇，論古今文體，引而次之。

translations.literal: Earlier Xie composed Literary Mind and Carved Dragon in fifty chapters, discussing styles of writing ancient and modern, citing and arranging them.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Literary Mind and Carved Dragon in fifty chapters on styles past and present.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface says:
translations.idiomatic: The preface says:

sentences.zh: 夫文心者，言爲文之用心也。

translations.literal: Literary Mind means the mind applied to writing.
translations.idiomatic: Literary Mind means mind applied to writing.

sentences.zh: 昔涓子《琴心》，王孫《巧心》，心哉美矣夫，故用之焉。

translations.literal: Long ago Juanzi had "Lute Mind" and Wang Sun "Clever Mind"—how beautiful the mind is! Hence I use it.
translations.idiomatic: Juanzi's Lute Mind and Wang Sun's Clever Mind show how beautiful mind is—hence the title.

sentences.zh: 古來文章，以雕縟成體，豈取騶奭羣言雕龍也。

translations.literal: Writings from antiquity take ornate carving as their form—does one take Zou Yi's many words and "carve the dragon"?
translations.idiomatic: Ancient writings are ornate—is the title from Zou Yi's "carving the dragon"?

sentences.zh: 夫宇宙綿邈，黎獻紛雜，拔萃出類，智術而已。

translations.literal: The cosmos is vast; the people numerous and mixed; to stand out from the crowd is a matter of intelligence alone.
translations.idiomatic: The cosmos is vast; to stand out takes intelligence alone.

sentences.zh: 歲月飄忽，性靈不居，騰聲飛實，製作而已。

translations.literal: Years and months flit; nature and spirit do not stay; to raise sound and solid achievement is a matter of making alone.
translations.idiomatic: Time flies; raising sound and fact is making alone.

sentences.zh: 夫肖貌天地，稟性五才，擬耳目於日月，方聲氣乎風雷，其超出萬物，亦已靈矣。

translations.literal: We mirror heaven and earth, receive the nature of the five talents, model ear and eye on sun and moon and square voice and breath on wind and thunder—we already surpass the ten thousand things in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: We mirror heaven and earth, model senses on sun and moon and voice on wind and thunder—we surpass all things in spirit.

sentences.zh: 形甚草木之脆，名逾金石之堅，是以君子處世，樹德建言，豈好辯哉？

translations.literal: Form is frailer than grass and trees; fame harder than metal and stone—therefore the gentleman in the world plants virtue and sets forth words: is it because he loves debate?
translations.idiomatic: Form is fragile, fame hard—gentlemen plant virtue and speak: not from love of debate

sentences.zh: 不得已也。

translations.literal: It is because he cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: but because they must.

sentences.zh: 予齒在逾立，嘗夜夢執丹漆之禮器，隨仲尼而南行，旦而寤，乃怡然而喜。

translations.literal: My teeth had passed twenty; once at night I dreamed I held vermilion-lacquered ritual vessels and followed Confucius south; waking at dawn I was pleased in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Past twenty I dreamed I held ritual vessels following Confucius south and woke pleased.

sentences.zh: 大哉聖人之難見也！

translations.literal: Great indeed is the difficulty of seeing the sage!
translations.idiomatic: How hard to see the sage!

sentences.zh: 乃小子之垂夢歟！

translations.literal: Was it the small man's dream granted below?
translations.idiomatic: Was it a small man's dream below?

sentences.zh: 自生人以來，未有如夫子者也。

translations.literal: Since men arose there has been none like the Master.
translations.idiomatic: Since men arose none like the Master.

sentences.zh: 敷贊聖旨，莫若注經，而馬、鄭諸儒，弘之已精，就有深解，未足立家。

translations.literal: To spread and praise the sage intent nothing surpasses annotating the classics; yet Ma, Zheng, and the Ru have already refined that; even deep understanding cannot establish a school.
translations.idiomatic: Annotating classics spreads the sage intent, but Ma and Zheng refined it—deep insight cannot found a school.

sentences.zh: 唯文章之用，實經典枝條，五禮資之以成，六典因之致用，君臣所以炳煥，軍國所以昭明。

translations.literal: Only the use of writing is truly branches of the classics: the five rites rely on it to form, the six canons use it to function; lord and minister thereby shine, army and state thereby clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Writing alone is the classics' branches: rites and canons depend on it; lord and minister and army and state shine through it.

sentences.zh: 詳其本源，莫非經典。

translations.literal: Examined to their root, none are not from the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At root all come from the classics.

sentences.zh: 而去聖久遠，文體解散，辭人愛奇，言貴浮詭，飾羽尚畫，文繡鞶帨，離本彌甚，將遂訛濫。

translations.literal: But departed from the sage long, styles dissolved; writers love the strange, words prize floating guile, adorn feathers and esteem paint, embroider saddle flaps—ever farther from the root, about to sink into false overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Far from sages, styles dissolved; writers loved the strange and ornament, drifting from root toward false overflow.

sentences.zh: 蓋《周書》論辭，貴乎體要；

translations.literal: The Zhou Documents discuss phrasing and prize substance;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Documents prize substance in phrasing;

sentences.zh: 尼父陳訓，惡乎異端。

translations.literal: Confucius in instruction hated heterodox branches.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius hated heterodox branches.

sentences.zh: 辭訓之異，宜體於要。

translations.literal: The difference of phrasing and instruction should take substance as body.
translations.idiomatic: Phrasing and instruction should take substance as body.

sentences.zh: 於是搦筆和墨，乃始論文。

translations.literal: Thereupon I took brush and ink and began to discuss writing.
translations.idiomatic: So I took brush and ink and began to discuss writing.

sentences.zh: 詳觀近代之論文者多矣。

translations.literal: I have looked closely at recent discussions of writing—there are many.
translations.idiomatic: Recent writing discussions are many.

sentences.zh: 至如魏文述《典》，陳思序《書》，應瑒《文論》，陸機《文賦》，仲洽《流別》，弘範《翰林》，各照隅隙，鮮觀衢路。

translations.literal: As for Cao Pi's "Classic" discourse, Chen Si's "Letter" preface, Ying Chang's Literary Discourse, Lu Ji's Literary Fu, Wang Zhongxuan's Genre Differentiation, Liu Hongfan's Forest of Letters—each illuminates a corner, rarely seeing the thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi's Classic, Cao Zhi's Letter, Ying Chang, Lu Ji, Wang Zhongxuan, Liu Hongfan—each sees a corner, rarely the road.

sentences.zh: 或臧否當時之才，或銓品前修之文，或汎舉雅俗之旨，或撮題篇章之意。

translations.literal: Some praise or blame the talent of the time, some weigh the writings of earlier masters, some broadly cite elegant and vulgar aims, some gather the meaning of titles and chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Some judge present talent, some earlier writings, some taste, some chapter themes.

sentences.zh: 魏《典》密而不周，陳《書》辯而無當，應《論》華而疏略，陸《賦》巧而碎亂，《流別》精而少功，《翰林》淺而寡要。

translations.literal: Wei's Classic is dense but not complete; Chen's Letter is clever but not sound; Ying's Discourse is florid but loose; Lu's Fu is artful but fragmented; Genre Differentiation is fine but slight in achievement; Forest of Letters is shallow and short on essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Classic is dense but incomplete; Chen's Letter clever but unsound; Ying loose; Lu fragmented; Genre Differentiation fine but slight; Forest shallow.

sentences.zh: 又君山、公幹之徒，吉甫、士龍之輩，汎議文意，往往間出，並未能振葉以尋根，觀瀾而索源。

translations.literal: Again Junshan, Gonggan, and company, Jifu, Shilong, and the like—floating discussion of literary intent often appears piecemeal, yet none could shake the leaf to seek the root or watch the billows to find the source.
translations.idiomatic: Junshan, Gonggan, Jifu, Shilong discuss in pieces but none sought root from leaf or source from billows.

sentences.zh: 不述先哲之誥，無益後生之慮。

translations.literal: They do not transmit the prior sages' instructions; they do not aid later students' thought.
translations.idiomatic: They do not transmit sages' instructions or aid later students.

sentences.zh: 蓋《文心》之作也，本乎道，師乎聖，體乎經，酌乎緯，變乎《騷》，文之樞紐，亦云極矣。

translations.literal: The making of Literary Mind roots in the Way, takes the sage as teacher, takes the classics as body, draws on the weft-texts, transforms with the "Li Sao"—the pivot of writing is thereby extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Literary Mind roots in the Way, sages, classics, weft-texts, and Li Sao—the pivot of writing.

sentences.zh: 若乃論文敘筆，則囿別區分，原始以表末，釋名以章義，選文以定篇，敷理以舉統；

translations.literal: As for discussing writing and narrating the brush, then delimiting and distinguishing, showing origin to display end, explaining names to clarify meaning, selecting texts to fix chapters, spreading principle to raise systems—
translations.idiomatic: It delimits writing, shows origin and end, names and meaning, texts and chapters, principle and systems—

sentences.zh: 上篇以上，綱領明矣。

translations.literal: in the upper chapters above, the outline is clear.
translations.idiomatic: the upper chapters' outline is clear.

sentences.zh: 至於割情析表，籠圈條貫，摛神性，圖風勢，苞會通，閱聲字，崇贊於《時序》，褒貶於《才略》，怊悵於《知音》，耿介於《程器》，長懷《序志》，以馭羣篇；

translations.literal: As for cutting emotion and analyzing expression, encircling principles, grasping spirit and nature, mapping wind and force, embracing convergence, surveying sound and character, exalting in "Seasonal Order," praising and blaming in "Talent Summary," sorrow in "Knowing Sound," integrity in "Style Vessel," long holding "Preface Intent" to drive the host of chapters—
translations.idiomatic: It cuts emotion, maps wind, surveys sound, exalts Seasonal Order, Talent Summary, Knowing Sound, Style Vessel, and Preface Intent—

sentences.zh: 下篇以下，毛目顯矣。

translations.literal: in the lower chapters below, the categories are manifest.
translations.idiomatic: the lower chapters' categories are manifest.

sentences.zh: 位理定名，彰乎《大易》之數，其爲文用，四十九篇而已。

translations.literal: Positioning principle and fixing names shine in the numbers of the Great Change; as use for writing, forty-nine chapters only.
translations.idiomatic: Principle and names shine in Change numbers; forty-nine chapters serve writing.

sentences.zh: 夫銓敘一文爲易，彌綸羣言爲難。

translations.literal: To weigh and narrate one text is easy; to bind the host of sayings is hard.
translations.idiomatic: One text is easy; binding all sayings is hard.

sentences.zh: 雖復輕采毛髮，深極骨髓，或有曲意密源，似近而遠，辭所不載，亦不勝數矣。

translations.literal: Though one plucks the hair lightly and probes the marrow deeply, some bend meaning in hidden sources, seeming near yet far—what the words do not carry cannot be numbered either.
translations.idiomatic: Though probing deep, hidden sources seem near yet far—much is left unsaid.

sentences.zh: 及其品評成文，有同乎舊談者，非雷同也，勢自不可異也；

translations.literal: When judging finished writing, some match old talk—not from mere sameness but because momentum cannot differ;
translations.idiomatic: Some judgments match old talk—not sameness but necessity;

sentences.zh: 有異乎前論者，非苟異也，理自不可同也。

translations.literal: some differ from prior discourse—not from rash difference but because principle cannot be the same.
translations.idiomatic: some differ—not rashness but different principle.

sentences.zh: 同之與異，不屑古今，擘肌分理，唯務折衷。

translations.literal: Sameness and difference pay no heed to ancient and modern; splitting muscle and dividing principle, one only seeks the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Sameness and difference ignore age; one seeks the mean.

sentences.zh: 案轡文雅之場，而環絡藻繪之府，亦幾乎備矣。

translations.literal: Holding the reins in the field of elegant letters and encircling the palace of ornament—one is almost complete.
translations.idiomatic: One almost completes the field of letters and ornament.

sentences.zh: 但言不盡意，聖人所難，識在缾管，何能矩矱。

translations.literal: But words do not exhaust meaning—the sage's difficulty; knowing is in the bottle tube—how can one square the compass?
translations.idiomatic: Words do not exhaust meaning; knowing is narrow—how square the compass?

sentences.zh: 茫茫往代，旣洗予聞；

translations.literal: Vast past ages have already washed my hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Past ages have washed my hearing;

sentences.zh: 眇眇來世，儻塵彼觀。

translations.literal: dim coming ages perhaps dust that view.
translations.idiomatic: coming ages may dust that view.

sentences.zh: 旣成，未爲時流所稱。

translations.literal: When finished, it was not praised by the currents of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Finished, it was not praised by the age.

sentences.zh: 勰自重其文，欲取定於沈約。

translations.literal: Xie himself prized his text and wished to fix it with Shen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Xie prized his text and sought Shen Yue's judgment.

sentences.zh: 約時貴盛，無由自達，乃負其書，候約出，干之於車前，狀若貨鬻者。

translations.literal: Yue was then noble and flourishing; there was no way to reach him, so he carried his book and waited for Yue to go out, accosting him before the carriage as if selling goods.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to reach noble Shen Yue, he waited at his carriage like a peddler.

sentences.zh: 約便命取讀，大重之，謂爲深得文理，常陳諸几案。

translations.literal: Yue at once ordered it taken and read, greatly valued it, said it deeply attained literary principle, and often set it on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: Yue read it, prized it, said it mastered principle, and kept it on his desk.

sentences.zh: 然勰爲文長於佛理，京師寺塔及名僧碑誌，必請勰制文。
