translations.literal: Yet Xie's writing excelled in Buddhist principle; capital temple towers and famous monks' steles and records always asked Xie to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in Buddhist writing; temples and steles sought his texts.

sentences.zh: 有敕與慧震沙門於定林寺撰經證，功畢，遂啓求出家，先燔鬢髮以自誓，敕許之。

translations.literal: An edict had him with the monk Huizhen at Dinglin compile sutra testimony; when the work was done he memorialized to leave the household, first burning his temple hair in vow; the edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile sutras with Huizhen, he then vowed to tonsure; the throne permitted it.

sentences.zh: 乃於寺變服，改名慧地。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the temple he changed robes and took the name Huidi.
translations.idiomatic: He changed robes at the temple and took the name Huidi.

sentences.zh: 未朞而卒。

translations.literal: Before a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he died.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works circulated.

sentences.zh: 王籍字文海，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, styled Wenhai, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, styled Wenhai, was from Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖遠，宋光祿勳。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yuan was Song Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yuan was Song director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 父僧祐，齊驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Father Sengyou was Qi Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Father Sengyou was Qi rapid cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 籍七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Ji at seven could compose.
translations.idiomatic: At seven Ji could compose.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學博涉，有才氣，樂安任昉見而稱之。

translations.literal: Grown, he loved learning and broad study, had talent and spirit; Le'an Ren Fang saw him and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he studied widely; Ren Fang praised him.

sentences.zh: 嘗於沈約坐賦得《詠燭》，甚爲約賞。

translations.literal: Once at Shen Yue's seat he was assigned to compose "On the Candle" and Yue greatly prized it.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen Yue's he composed On the Candle and won praise.

sentences.zh: 齊末，爲冠軍行參軍，累遷外兵、記室。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi he was Champion acting aide, rising repeatedly to external affairs and staff secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Late Qi he was champion aide, then external affairs and staff secretary.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除安成王主簿、尚書三公郎、廷尉正。

translations.literal: Early Tianjian he was made Prince of Ancheng chief clerk, Secretariat third-rank gentleman, and Court Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was Ancheng chief clerk, secretariat gentleman, and court reviewer.

sentences.zh: 歷餘姚、錢塘令，並以放免。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yuyao and Qiantang, both dismissed for license.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yuyao and Qiantang, both dismissed for license.

sentences.zh: 久之，除輕車湘東王諮議參軍，隨府會稽。

translations.literal: After long time he was made Light Chariot Prince Xiangdong consulting colonel and followed the princedom to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Xiangdong consulting colonel in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 郡境有雲門、天柱山，籍嘗遊之，或累月不反。

translations.literal: Within the commandery were Cloud Gate and Tianzhu mountains; Ji often toured them, sometimes not returning for months.
translations.idiomatic: He often toured Cloud Gate and Tianzhu for months.

sentences.zh: 至若邪溪賦詩，其略云：「蟬噪林逾靜，鳥鳴山更幽。

translations.literal: At Ruoye Creek composing poetry, the gist said: "Cicadas cry—the grove is stiller; birds call—the mountain more secluded."
translations.idiomatic: At Ruoye Creek: "Cicadas cry—the grove stiller; birds call—the mountain more secluded."

sentences.zh: 」當時以爲文外獨絕。

translations.literal: The age took it as uniquely beyond the text.
translations.idiomatic: The age called it beyond the text.

sentences.zh: 還爲大司馬從事中郎，遷中散大夫，尤不得志，遂徒行市道，不擇交遊。

translations.literal: Returning he was Grand Marshal attendant gentleman, promoted to Palace Regular Grandee; especially frustrated, he then walked the market lanes on foot, not choosing company.
translations.idiomatic: Returning frustrated, he walked markets without choosing company.

sentences.zh: 湘東王爲荊州，引爲安西府諮議參軍，帶作塘令。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong was in Jingzhou and summoned him as Anxi consulting colonel, concurrently magistrate of Zuotang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangdong in Jingzhou made him consulting colonel and Zuotang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 不理縣事，日飲酒，人有訟者，鞭而遣之。

translations.literal: He did not handle county affairs, drank daily; when men sued he whipped and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He drank daily; suitors he whipped away.

sentences.zh: 少時，卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works circulated.

sentences.zh: 子碧，亦有文才，先籍卒。

translations.literal: Son Bi also had literary talent and died before Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Son Bi had talent and died before Ji.

sentences.zh: 何思澄字元靜，東海郯人。

translations.literal: He Sicheng, styled Yuanjing, was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Sicheng, styled Yuanjing, was from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 父敬叔，齊征東錄事參軍、餘杭令。

translations.literal: Father Jingshu was Qi Eastern Expedition recorder and Yuhang magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Father Jingshu was Qi eastern expedition recorder and Yuhang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 思澄少勤學，工文辭。

translations.literal: Sicheng in youth studied diligently and was skilled at literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Young Sicheng studied hard and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 起家爲南康王侍郎，累遷安成王左常侍，兼太學博士，平南安成王行參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: He began as Prince of Nankang gentleman, rising to Prince of Ancheng left regular attendant, concurrently National University erudite, Pingnan Prince of Ancheng acting aide, concurrently staff secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He began in Nankang service, rose to Ancheng attendant, erudite, and staff secretary.

sentences.zh: 隨府江州，爲《遊廬山詩》，沈約見之，大相稱賞，自以爲弗逮。

translations.literal: Following the princedom to Jiangzhou he made "Poem on Touring Mount Lu"; Shen Yue saw it and greatly praised it, himself thinking he did not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: His Mount Lu poem made Shen Yue praise him above himself.

sentences.zh: 約郊居宅新構閣齋，因命工書人題此詩於壁。

translations.literal: Yue's suburban residence newly built a tower study; he ordered a scribe to inscribe this poem on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had the poem inscribed on his new tower study.

sentences.zh: 傅昭常請思澄制《釋奠詩》，辭文典麗。

translations.literal: Fu Zhao often asked Sicheng to compose "Sacrifice to the Master" poetry; the diction was classic and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhao asked for Sacrifice poetry—classic and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 除廷尉正。

translations.literal: He was made Court Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He became court reviewer.

sentences.zh: 天監十五年，敕太子詹事徐勉舉學士入華林撰《遍略》，勉舉思澄等五人以應選。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian an edict ordered Crown Prince Grand Tutor Xu Mian to recommend scholars to enter Hualin and compile the Comprehensive Digest; Mian recommended Sicheng and four others to answer the selection.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year fifteen Mian recommended Sicheng and four others for Hualin Digest.

sentences.zh: 遷治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊以來，此職稍輕，天監初始重其選。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi this post had grown somewhat light; at the beginning of Tianjian they first again weighted the choice.
translations.idiomatic: The post had grown light; Tianjian restored its weight.

sentences.zh: 車前依尚書二丞給三騶，執盛印青囊，舊事糾彈官印綬在前故也。

translations.literal: Before the carriage, following the two Ministry of Works aides, three outriders were given, holding the seal pouch in blue bag—old business because the impeaching officer's seal cords went in front.
translations.idiomatic: Three outriders and seal pouch followed old impeachment custom.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷秣陵令，入兼東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: After long time he was promoted to Moling magistrate, entered concurrently as Eastern Palace Communications Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later Moling magistrate and Eastern Palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 除安西湘東王錄事參軍，兼舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was made Anxi Prince Xiangdong recorder, still Communications Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was Xiangdong recorder while keeping attendant duty.

sentences.zh: 時徐勉、周捨以才具當朝，並好思澄學，常遞日招致之。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Mian and Zhou She with talent held the court and both loved Sicheng's learning, often inviting him day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian and Zhou She, holding court, often invited him.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子薨，出爲黟縣令。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died he went out as magistrate of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoming died he became Yi magistrate.

sentences.zh: 遷除宣惠武陵王中錄事參軍，卒官，時年五十四。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Xuanhui Prince of Wuling center recorder and died in office at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Wuling center recorder and died in office at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 文集十五卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen scrolls of works.

sentences.zh: 初，思澄與宗人遜及子朗俱擅文名，時人語曰：「東海三何，子朗最多。

translations.literal: Earlier Sicheng with clansman Xun and son Lang all had literary fame; people of the time said: "The three He of Donghai—son Lang the most."
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Three He of Donghai—son Lang most."

sentences.zh: 」思澄聞之，曰：「此言誤耳。

translations.literal: Sicheng heard it and said: "This saying is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng said: "That is wrong."

sentences.zh: 如其不然，故當歸遜。

translations.literal: If not so, it should go to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: If not, it belongs to Xun.

sentences.zh: 」思澄意謂宜在己也。

translations.literal: Sicheng's intent was that it should be on himself.
translations.idiomatic: He meant himself.

sentences.zh: 子朗字世明，早有才思，工清言，周捨每與共談，服其精理。

translations.literal: Son Lang, styled Shiming, early had talent and thought, excelled in pure talk; Zhou She often discussed with him and admired his subtle principle.
translations.idiomatic: Son Lang, styled Shiming, excelled in pure talk; Zhou She admired him.

sentences.zh: 嘗爲《敗冢賦》，擬莊周馬棰，其文甚工。

translations.literal: Once he made "Rhapsody on the Ruined Mound," modeled on Zhuang Zhou's horse whip; the text was very artful.
translations.idiomatic: His Ruined Mound rhapsody modeled Zhuangzi—very artful.

sentences.zh: 世人語曰：「人中爽爽何子朗。

translations.literal: People of the world said: "Among men, bright bright He Zilang."
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Among men, bright He Zilang."

sentences.zh: 」歷官員外散騎侍郎，出爲固山令。

translations.literal: He served as Supernumerary Cavalry Gentleman and went out as magistrate of Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was supernumerary cavalry gentleman and Gushan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年二十四。

translations.literal: He died at age twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works circulated.

sentences.zh: 劉杳字士深，平原平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Cha, styled Shishen, was a man of Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cha, styled Shishen, was from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖乘民，宋冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Chenmin was Song Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Chenmin was Song Ji inspector.

sentences.zh: 父聞慰，齊東陽太守，有清績，在《齊書·良政傳》。

translations.literal: Father Wenwei was Qi Administrator of Dongyang; he had pure achievement and is in the "Biography of Good Administration" of the Book of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Father Wenwei was Qi Dongyang administrator, in Qi's Good Administration biography.

sentences.zh: 杳年數歲，徵士明僧紹見之，撫而言曰：「此兒實千里之駒。

translations.literal: Cha at several years—Recluse Ming Sengshao saw him, stroked him and said: "This boy is truly a thousand-li colt."
translations.idiomatic: Sengshao called young Cha a thousand-li colt.

sentences.zh: 」十三，丁父憂，每哭，哀感行路。

translations.literal: At thirteen he entered his father's mourning; each time he wept his grief moved passersby.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen mourning his father, his weeping moved passersby.

sentences.zh: 天監初，爲太學博士、宣惠豫章王行參軍。

translations.literal: Early Tianjian he was National University erudite and Xuanhui Prince of Yuzhang acting aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was university erudite and Yuzhang acting aide.

sentences.zh: 杳少好學，博綜羣書，沈約、任昉以下，每有遺忘，皆訪問焉。

translations.literal: Cha in youth loved learning, broadly mastering many books; from Shen Yue and Ren Fang down, whenever they forgot something they all consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered many books; Shen Yue and Ren Fang consulted him on forgettings.

sentences.zh: 嘗於約坐語及宗廟犧樽，約云：「鄭玄答張逸，謂爲畫鳳皇尾娑娑然。

translations.literal: Once at Yue's seat they spoke of the ancestral temple victim-vessel; Yue said: "Zheng Xuan answering Zhang Yi said it was painting a phoenix tail swaying.
translations.idiomatic: At Yue's they discussed the victim-vessel; Yue cited Zheng Xuan on a painted phoenix tail.

sentences.zh: 今無復此器，則不依古。

translations.literal: Today that vessel no longer exists, so one does not follow antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Today it no longer exists, so we do not follow antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」杳曰：「此言未必可按。

translations.literal: Cha said: "This saying cannot necessarily be pressed."
translations.idiomatic: Cha said: "That cannot be pressed."

sentences.zh: 古者樽彝，皆刻木爲鳥獸，鑿頂及背，以出內酒。

translations.literal: In antiquity sacrificial vessels were all carved wood as birds and beasts, boring the top and back to draw out the inner wine.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient vessels were carved birds and beasts with bored tops for wine.

sentences.zh: 頃魏世魯郡地中得齊大夫子尾送女器，有犧樽作犧牛形；

translations.literal: Recently in Wei times in Lu commandery underground they obtained Qi grandee Ziwei's daughter-send-off vessels, with a victim-vessel in victim-ox form;
translations.idiomatic: Wei times in Lu yielded Qi vessels with an ox-shaped victim-vessel;

sentences.zh: 晉永嘉賊曹嶷於青州發齊景公冢，又得此二樽，形亦爲牛象。

translations.literal: in the Yongjia era the bandit Cao Yi at Qingzhou opened Duke Jing of Qi's tomb and again obtained these two vessels, the form also ox-shaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia bandit Cao Yi opened Duke Jing's tomb and found two ox-shaped vessels.

sentences.zh: 二處皆古之遺器，知非虛也。

translations.literal: Both places are ancient surviving vessels; one knows it is not empty.
translations.idiomatic: Both are ancient vessels—proof, not fiction.

sentences.zh: 」約大以爲然。

translations.literal: Yue greatly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue agreed fully.

sentences.zh: 約又云：「何承天《纂文》奇博，其書載張仲師及長頸王事，此何出？

translations.literal: Yue also said: "He Chengtian's Collected Texts is strange and broad; the book records Zhang Zhongshi and the long-neck king—where does this come from?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue asked where He Chengtian's Zhang Zhongshi and long-neck king came from.

sentences.zh: 」杳曰：「仲師長尺二寸，唯出《論衡》。

translations.literal: Cha said: "Zhongshi was one foot two inches long—only from the Discourses Weighed."
translations.idiomatic: Cha said Zhongshi's height is only in Discourses Weighed.

sentences.zh: 長頸是毘騫王，朱建安《扶南以南記》云：古來至今不死。

translations.literal: The long neck is King Virudhaka; Zhu Jian's Record South of Funan says: from antiquity to now he does not die."
translations.idiomatic: The long neck is King Virudhaka in Zhu Jian's Record south of Funan—immortal from antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」約即取二書尋檢，一如杳言。

translations.literal: Yue at once took the two books and searched; it was exactly as Cha said.
translations.idiomatic: Yue searched both books—exactly as Cha said.

sentences.zh: 約郊居宅時新構閣齋，杳爲贊二首，並以所撰文章呈約，約即命工書人題其贊于壁。

translations.literal: When Yue's suburban residence newly built the tower study, Cha made two encomia and also presented writings he had composed; Yue at once ordered a scribe to inscribe the encomia on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Cha gave two encomia for Yue's tower study; Yue had them inscribed.

sentences.zh: 仍報杳書曰：「生平愛嗜，不在人中，林壑之歡，多與事奪。

translations.literal: He still replied to Cha in a letter saying: "Life's loves are not among men; joy of forests and ravines is much stolen by affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue wrote: "Life's loves are not among men; ravine joy is stolen by affairs.

sentences.zh: 日暮塗殫，此心往矣；

translations.literal: Sunset on the road ends—this heart has gone;
translations.idiomatic: Sunset ends the road—my heart has gone;

sentences.zh: 猶復少存閑遠，徵懷清曠。

translations.literal: yet still a little idle distance remains, summoning feelings clear and spacious.
translations.idiomatic: yet a little idle distance and clear feelings remain.

sentences.zh: 結宇東郊，匪云止息，政復頗寄夙心，時得休偃。

translations.literal: I built a house in the eastern suburbs—not called stopping rest, but rather it quite lodges my old heart, sometimes allowing repose."
translations.idiomatic: I built in the eastern suburbs—not mere rest but lodging my old heart for repose."

sentences.zh: 仲長游居之地，休璉所述之美，望慕空深，何可髣髴。

translations.literal: The place where Zhongchang You dwelt in retirement and the beauty Xiu Lian described—my longing runs deep and empty; how could one even sketch it?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchang You's retreat and Xiu Lian's praise left me yearning with no likeness.

sentences.zh: 君愛素情多，惠以二贊。

translations.literal: You love plain feeling greatly and have favored me with two encomia.
translations.idiomatic: Your generous gift of two encomia shows how much you cherish plain feeling.

sentences.zh: 辭采妍富，事義畢舉，句韻之間，光影相照，便覺此地，自然十倍。

translations.literal: The diction is rich and lovely, the matter and meaning fully set forth; between lines and rhymes light and shadow answer each other—suddenly this place seems ten times itself by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Lovely diction, full meaning, line answering line in light—this place seems tenfold brighter.

sentences.zh: 故知麗辭之益，其事弘多，輒當置之閣上，坐臥嗟覽。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the benefit of fine words is vast; I shall place them on the upper shelf and sigh over them sitting or lying down.
translations.idiomatic: Fine words help so much—I will keep them on the shelf and read them again and again.

sentences.zh: 別卷諸篇，並爲名制。

translations.literal: The other scrolls and pieces are all famous compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Your other pieces are all masterworks.

sentences.zh: 又山寺旣爲警策，諸賢從時復高奇，解頤愈疾，義兼乎此。

translations.literal: Again, the mountain-temple piece is already a sharp admonition; the gentlemen's pieces of the time are again lofty and strange—delighting the cheek and curing illness; the meaning joins with this.
translations.idiomatic: Your mountain-temple essay already warns; your friends' pieces are lofty too—joy and healing together.

sentences.zh: 遲此敘會，更共申析。

translations.literal: Delay this meeting for talk; let us analyze together again.
translations.idiomatic: Let us meet soon and discuss them further.

sentences.zh: 」其爲約所賞如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he prized by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue prized him in this way.

sentences.zh: 又在任昉坐，有人餉昉𣒅酒而作榐字。

translations.literal: Again, once at Ren Fang's seat someone presented Fang with jujube wine and wrote the character with the "wood" form.
translations.idiomatic: At Ren Fang's seat someone sent jujube wine and wrote the character with a wood radical.

sentences.zh: 昉問杳：「此字是不？

translations.literal: Fang asked Cha: "Is this character correct?"
translations.idiomatic: Fang asked Cha whether the character was right.

sentences.zh: 」杳對曰：「葛洪《字苑》作木旁𠯌。

translations.literal: Cha replied: "Ge Hong's Character Garden writes it with wood beside 朌."
translations.idiomatic: Cha said Ge Hong's Character Garden puts wood beside 朌.

sentences.zh: 」昉又曰：「酒有千日醉，當是虛言。

translations.literal: Fang also said: "Wine that makes one drunk a thousand days must be empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: Fang also said thousand-day drunkenness must be fiction.

sentences.zh: 」杳云：「桂陽程鄉有千里酒，飲之至家而醉，亦其例也。

translations.literal: Cha said: "In Guiyang's Chengxiang there is thousand-li wine; drink it and you are drunk when you reach home—that is also an example."
translations.idiomatic: Cha said Guiyang's Chengxiang had thousand-li wine that left you drunk at home—another example.

sentences.zh: 」昉大驚曰：「吾自當遺忘，實不憶此。

translations.literal: Fang was greatly startled and said: "I must have forgotten myself; I truly do not recall this."
translations.idiomatic: Fang was startled: "I must have forgotten; I truly do not recall this."

sentences.zh: 」杳云：「出楊元鳳所撰《置郡事》。

translations.literal: Cha said: "It comes from Yang Yuanfeng's compiled Record of Establishing Commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: Cha said it came from Yang Yuanfeng's Record of Establishing Commanderies.

sentences.zh: 元鳳是魏代人，此書仍載其賦，云三重五品，商溪摖里。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng was a man of Wei; that book still carries his fu, saying "triple ranks and five grades, Shangxi and Zeli."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng was a Wei man; the book still has his fu on triple ranks and five grades at Shangxi and Zeli.

sentences.zh: 」時即檢楊記，言皆不差。

translations.literal: They immediately checked Yang's record; every word matched.
translations.idiomatic: They checked Yang's record at once; all matched.

sentences.zh: 王僧孺被敕撰譜，訪杳血脈所因。

translations.literal: Wang Sengru received an edict to compile genealogies and asked Cha about the origins of blood lines.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru, ordered to compile genealogies, asked Cha about blood-line origins.

sentences.zh: 杳云：「桓譚《新論》云：『太史《三代世表》，旁行邪上，並效周譜。

translations.literal: Cha said: "Huan Tan's New Discourses says: 'The Grand Historian's Genealogical Tables of Three Ages run sideways and slant upward, all imitating Zhou genealogies.'"
translations.idiomatic: Cha cited Huan Tan: the Grand Historian's tables ran sideways like Zhou genealogies.

sentences.zh: 』以此而推，當起周代。

translations.literal: By this one infers they must begin in the Zhou era.
translations.idiomatic: From that he inferred they began in Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」僧孺歎曰：「可謂得所未聞。

translations.literal: Sengru sighed and said: "One may say this is something never heard before."
translations.idiomatic: Sengru sighed: "Truly unheard-of."

sentences.zh: 」周捨又問杳：「尚書官著紫荷橐，相傳云『挈囊』，竟何所出？

translations.literal: Zhou She also asked Cha: "Attendants-in-ordinary wear purple lotus pouches; tradition says 'grasping the pouch'—where does it ultimately come from?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She asked why attendants-in-ordinary wore purple lotus pouches—the "grasping the pouch" tradition.

sentences.zh: 」杳答曰：「《張安世傳》曰『持橐簪筆，事孝武皇帝數十年』。

translations.literal: Cha answered: "The Biography of Zhang Anshi says 'holding the pouch and pinning the brush, serving Emperor Xiaowu for several decades.'"
translations.idiomatic: Cha cited Zhang Anshi's biography on holding pouch and brush for decades.

sentences.zh: 韋昭、張晏注並云『橐，囊也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao's and Zhang Yan's commentaries both say 'pouch means bag.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao and Zhang Yan both glossed pouch as bag.

sentences.zh: 近臣簪筆，以待顧問』。

translations.literal: A close minister pins the brush to await consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Close ministers pinned brushes to await consultation.

sentences.zh: 」范岫撰《字書音訓》，又訪杳焉。

translations.literal: Fan Xiu compiled Pronunciation and Glosses for the Character Book and again consulted Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiu, compiling pronunciation glosses, consulted Cha again.

sentences.zh: 其博識強記，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His broad learning and strong memory were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His erudition and memory were all like this.

sentences.zh: 尋佐周捨撰國史。

translations.literal: Soon he assisted Zhou She in compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he assisted Zhou She on the national history.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨津令，有善績。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Linjin and had good achievements.
translations.idiomatic: As Linjin magistrate he achieved good results.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，縣人三百餘人詣闕請留，敕許焉。

translations.literal: When his term ended, more than three hundred men of the county went to the gate to ask that he be kept; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end three hundred county men petitioned to keep him; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 杳以疾陳解，還除雲麾晉安王府參軍。

translations.literal: Cha cited illness and asked to be released, then was appointed again as Cloud-Banner Prince Jin'an's staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Illness made him resign; he returned as Prince Jin'an's staff officer.

sentences.zh: 詹事徐勉舉杳及顧協等五人入華林撰《遍略》，書成，以本官兼廷尉正，又以足疾解。

translations.literal: Household Steward Xu Mian recommended Cha and Gu Xie and four others to enter Hualin to compile the Comprehensive Digest; when the book was finished he held his original office concurrently as Director of the Court of Justice, then resigned again because of foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian sent Cha and Gu Xie and others to Hualin for the Comprehensive Digest; afterward he was concurrent director of justice, then quit for foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 因著《林庭賦》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the "Forest Garden Fu."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote the "Forest Garden Fu."

sentences.zh: 王僧孺見之歎曰：「《郊居》以後，無復此作。

translations.literal: Wang Sengru, seeing it, sighed: "After the 'Suburban Dwelling' there is no such work again."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru sighed: "Nothing like this since the 'Suburban Dwelling.'"

sentences.zh: 」普通元年，復除建康正，遷尚書駕部郎；

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he was again appointed Director of Jiankang, then promoted to Director of the Imperial Stud;
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 he was Jiankang director, then imperial stud director;

sentences.zh: 數月，徙署儀曹郎，僕射勉以臺閣文議專委杳焉。

translations.literal: after several months he was transferred to act as Director of Ceremonies; Vice Minister Mian entrusted all court literary deliberations to Cha alone.
translations.idiomatic: months later he acted as director of ceremonies; Mian entrusted all literary business to him.

sentences.zh: 出爲餘姚令，在縣清潔，人有饋遺，一無所受，湘東王發教褒稱之。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Yuyao; in the county he was pure and clean, accepting nothing from anyone who offered gifts; Prince Xiangdong issued a commendation praising him.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuyao magistrate he was pure and took no gifts; Prince Xiangdong praised him.

sentences.zh: 還除宣惠湘東王記室參軍，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Returning, he was appointed Staff Officer to the Prince of Xuanhui, Prince Xiangdong, and left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Prince Xiangdong's staff officer, then mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復爲王府記室，兼東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became the prince's staff officer, concurrently Eastern Palace Attendant for Miscellaneous Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was staff officer again and eastern-palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，遷步兵校尉，兼舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers, still concurrently attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1 he became footsoldier commandant, still attendant.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子謂杳曰：「酒非卿所好，而爲酒廚之職，政爲不愧古人耳。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming said to Cha: "Wine is not what you love, yet you hold the office of wine steward—truly you do not shame the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said: "You dislike wine yet hold the wine office—you shame no ancients."

sentences.zh: 」俄有敕，代裴子野知著作郎事。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict having him replace Pei Ziye in charge of the Director of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict had him replace Pei Ziye as director of writings.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子薨，新宮建，舊人例無停者，敕特留杳焉。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died and the new palace was built, by old rule former staff were not kept; an edict specially retained Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoming died and the new palace rose, old staff were dismissed—but Cha was kept by edict.

sentences.zh: 仍注太子《徂歸賦》，稱爲博悉。

translations.literal: He also annotated the crown prince's "Fu on Returning," and was called thorough in knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the crown prince's "Fu on Returning" and was called thorough.

sentences.zh: 僕射何敬容奏轉杳王府諮議，高祖曰：「劉杳須先經中書。

translations.literal: Vice Minister He Jingrong memorialized to transfer Cha to the prince's staff counselor; Gaozu said: "Liu Cha must first pass through the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: He Jingrong wanted Cha as prince counselor; Gaozu said he must pass the secretariat first.

sentences.zh: 」仍除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尋爲平西湘東王諮議參軍，兼舍人、知著作如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was Pacifying-West Prince Xiangdong's staff counselor, concurrently attendant and in charge of writings as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Xiangdong's pacifying-west counselor, still attendant and director of writings.

sentences.zh: 遷爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，卒官，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died in office at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 2 he died in office at fifty.

sentences.zh: 杳治身清儉，無所嗜好。

translations.literal: Cha governed himself in purity and frugality and had no indulgences.
translations.idiomatic: Cha lived purely and frugally without indulgence.

sentences.zh: 爲性不自伐，不論人短長，及睹釋氏經教，常行慈忍。

translations.literal: By nature he did not boast; he did not discuss others' faults and strengths; when he saw Buddhist sutras he constantly practiced compassion and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He did not boast or judge others; Buddhist texts moved him to compassion.

sentences.zh: 天監十七年，自居母憂，便長斷腥膻，持齋蔬食。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianjian, from the time he mourned his mother, he long cut off meat and fish and kept vegetarian fast.
translations.idiomatic: From mourning his mother in Tianjian 17 he ate no meat and kept vegetarian fast.

sentences.zh: 及臨終，遺命斂以法服，載以露車，還葬舊墓，隨得一地，容棺而已，不得設靈筵祭醊。

translations.literal: At the end he left instructions to be dressed in monastic robes, carried on an open cart, and buried in the old tomb with only enough ground for the coffin; spirit tables and sacrificial feasts were not to be set up.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he ordered monastic dress, an open cart, a simple grave, and no spirit table or feast.

sentences.zh: 其子遵行之。

translations.literal: His son Zun carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zun obeyed.

sentences.zh: 杳自少至長，多所著述。

translations.literal: From youth to age Cha composed many works.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age he wrote much.

sentences.zh: 撰《要雅》五卷、《楚辭草木疏》一卷、《高士傳》二卷、《東宮新舊記》三十卷、《古今四部書目》五卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Essential Elegantiae in five juan, Exegesis of Plants in the Songs of Chu in one juan, Biographies of Lofty Men in two juan, Old and New Records of the Eastern Palace in thirty juan, and Catalogue of Books in Four Divisions, Ancient and Modern, in five juan—all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Essential Elegantiae (5 j.), Chu plants (1 j.), Lofty Men (2 j.), Eastern Palace records (30 j.), and a four-division catalogue (5 j.)—all extant.

sentences.zh: 謝徵字玄度，陳郡陽夏人。

translations.literal: Xie Zheng, courtesy name Xuandu, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zheng, styled Xuandu, was from Yangxia in Chen.

sentences.zh: 高祖景仁，宋尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor for the dynasty Jingren was Song Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty founder Jingren was Song left vice director.

sentences.zh: 祖稚，宋司徒主簿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi was Song Director of the Secretariat Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Zhi was Song secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 父璟，少與從叔朓俱知名。

translations.literal: His father Jing was young when he and his cousin Tiao were both famous.
translations.idiomatic: Father Jing and cousin Tiao were both famous young.

sentences.zh: 齊竟陵王子良開西邸，招文學，璟亦預焉。

translations.literal: In Qi, Prince Jingling of Jingling opened the Western Lodge to recruit men of letters; Jing also took part.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, Prince Jingling's western lodge drew writers; Jing joined them.

sentences.zh: 隆昌中，爲明帝驃騎諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: In Longchang he was staff counselor to Mingdi's Rapid Cavalry general, heading the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang he was Mingdi's rapid-cavalry counselor and headed the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，晉安內史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Interior Minister of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretariat gentleman and Jin'an interior minister.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京邑，爲霸府諮議、梁臺黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital region he was staff counselor to the Lord of Hegemony and Huangmen Gentleman of the Liang Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital he was hegemon counselor and Liang terrace huangmen gentleman.

sentences.zh: 天監初，累遷司農卿、秘書監、左民尚書、明威將軍、東陽太守。

translations.literal: In the early Tianjian era he was promoted in succession to Director of the Imperial Granaries, Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Left Household, General of Illustrious Might, and Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he rose through granaries, secretariat, left household, illustrious might general, and Dongyang grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 高祖用爲侍中，固辭年老，求金紫，未序，會疾卒。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to use him as Attendant-in-ordinary; he firmly declined on grounds of age and sought gold and purple rank; before the order was issued he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wanted him as attendant-in-ordinary; he declined for age and sought gold-purple rank, then died before appointment.

sentences.zh: 徵幼聰慧，璟異之，常謂親從曰：「此兒非常器，所憂者壽；

translations.literal: Zheng was clever as a child; Jing marveled at him and often told close kin: "This boy is no ordinary vessel; what I worry about is his lifespan;
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a child, Jing told kin: "This boy is extraordinary; I only fear a short life;

sentences.zh: 若天假其年，吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: if Heaven grants him years, I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: if Heaven grants years, I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 」旣長，美風采，好學善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he had fine bearing, loved learning, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he had fine bearing, loved learning, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 初爲安西安成王法曹，遷尚書金部三公二曹郎、豫章王記室，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: At first he was Law Officer to the Prince of An'an, Prince Ancheng; he was promoted to Gentleman of the Gold Bureau and the Three Dukes in the Masters of Writing and Staff Officer to the Prince of Yuzhang, concurrently Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Ancheng's law officer, then masters-of-writing gentleman and Yuzhang staff officer and secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷除平北諮議參軍，兼鴻臚卿，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted and removed to Pacifying-North staff counselor, concurrently Director of the Court for Dependencies, still attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He became pacifying-north counselor and director of dependencies, still attendant.

sentences.zh: 徵與河東裴子野、沛國劉顯同官友善，子野嘗爲《寒夜直宿賦》以贈徵，徵爲《感友賦》以酬之。

translations.literal: Zheng was on friendly terms with Hedong Pei Ziye and Pei Guo Liu Xian in the same office; Ziye once composed "Fu on Night Duty in the Cold" to present to Zheng, and Zheng composed "Fu on Moved by Friends" in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng befriended Pei Ziye and Liu Xian; they exchanged fu on night duty and friendship.

sentences.zh: 時魏中山王元略還北，高祖餞於武德殿，賦詩三十韻，限三刻成。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Prince Yuan Lue of Zhongshan was returning north; Gaozu feasted him at Wude Hall and assigned a poem of thirty rhymes to be finished within three quarter-hours.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei's Prince Yuan Lue left north, Gaozu feasted him at Wude and set a thirty-rhyme poem in three quarters of an hour.

sentences.zh: 徵二刻便就，其辭甚美，高祖再覽焉。

translations.literal: Zheng finished in two quarter-hours; the wording was very fine, and Gaozu read it twice.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng finished in two quarters; Gaozu read it twice.

sentences.zh: 又爲臨汝侯淵猷制《放生文》，亦見賞於世。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Essay on Releasing Life" for the Marquis of Linru, Yuan You, and it too was prized in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His "Essay on Releasing Life" for Marquis Yuan You was also prized.

sentences.zh: 臧嚴字彥威，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Zang Yan, courtesy name Yanwei, was a man of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Yan, styled Yanwei, was from Ju in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖燾，宋左光祿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tao was Song Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Tao was Song left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 祖凝，齊尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ning was Qi Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Ning was Qi right vice director.

sentences.zh: 父稜，後軍參軍。

translations.literal: His father Ling was Rear Army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Father Ling was rear army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 嚴幼有孝性，居父憂以毀聞。

translations.literal: Yan from childhood had filial nature; in mourning his father he was known for grief that injured him.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was filial; mourning his father he was known for destructive grief.

sentences.zh: 孤貧勤學，行止書卷不離於手。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he studied diligently; going and stopping, books never left his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he studied hard and always carried a book.

sentences.zh: 初爲安成王侍郎，轉常侍。

translations.literal: At first he was Gentleman to the Prince of Ancheng, then transferred to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Prince Ancheng's gentleman, then regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 從叔未甄爲江夏郡，攜嚴之官，於塗作《屯遊賦》，任昉見而稱之。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Wei Zhen was Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and took Yan to his post; on the road he composed the "Fu on Garrison Travel"; Ren Fang saw it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Wei Zhen took him to Jiangxia; on the road he wrote "Fu on Garrison Travel" and Ren Fang praised it.

sentences.zh: 又作《七算》，辭亦富麗。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Seven Calculations"; the wording too was rich and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: His "Seven Calculations" was also rich and lovely.

sentences.zh: 性孤介，於人間未嘗造請。

translations.literal: By nature he was solitary and aloof; among men he never paid calls.
translations.idiomatic: Solitary by nature, he never paid social calls.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉欲識之，嚴終不詣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Xu Mian wished to know him; Yan to the end did not visit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian wished to know him; Yan never came.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍行參軍、侍湘東王讀，累遷王宣惠輕車府參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Army Adjutant in the Champion's office and attended Prince Xiangdong's studies, then in succession to the prince's Xuanhui Light-Carriage staff officer, concurrently secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to champion adjutant, tutored Xiangdong, then light-carriage staff officer and secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嚴於學多所諳記，尤精《漢書》，諷誦略皆上口。

translations.literal: Yan in learning knew and remembered much, especially mastering the Book of Han; he could recite nearly all of it by heart.
translations.idiomatic: He knew much, especially the Book of Han, nearly all by heart.

sentences.zh: 王嘗自執四部書目以試之，嚴自甲至丁卷中，各對一事，並作者姓名，遂無遺失，其博洽如此。

translations.literal: The prince once himself held the catalogue of the four divisions to test him; from juan A through D in each volume Yan answered one item and the author's name, with nothing lost—so broadly learned was he.
translations.idiomatic: The prince tested him with the four-division catalogue; from A to D he named every item and author without error.

sentences.zh: 王遷荊州，隨府轉西中郎安西錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When the prince moved to Jingzhou, he followed the headquarters and became Recorder of the Western Central and Pacifying-West headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince went to Jingzhou he became western headquarters recorder.

sentences.zh: 歷監義陽、武寧郡，累任皆蠻左，前郡守常選武人，以兵鎮之；

translations.literal: He served in succession as Inspector of Yiyang and Wuning commanderies; successive posts were all on the barbarian frontier; former grand administrators often chose military men to hold them with troops;
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Yiyang and Wuning on the frontier where former magistrates used soldiers;

sentences.zh: 嚴獨以數門生單車入境，羣蠻悅服，遂絕寇盜。

translations.literal: Yan alone entered the territory with a few students in a single cart; the barbarian clans were pleased and submitted, and banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan entered alone with a few students; the tribes submitted and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 王入爲石頭戍軍事，除安右錄事。

translations.literal: When the prince entered the capital as military affairs officer at Stone City, he was appointed Pacifying-Right recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered as Stone City officer he was pacifying-right recorder.

sentences.zh: 王遷江州，爲鎮南諮議參軍，卒官。

translations.literal: When the prince moved to Jiangzhou he was Pacifying-South staff counselor and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou he was pacifying-south counselor and died in office.

sentences.zh: 文集十卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings were ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Collected writings: ten juan.

sentences.zh: 伏挺字士標。

translations.literal: Fu Ting, courtesy name Shibiao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ting, styled Shibiao.

sentences.zh: 父芃，爲豫章內史，在《良吏傳》。

translations.literal: His father Peng was Interior Minister of Yuzhang and appears in the Biography of Good Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Father Peng was Yuzhang interior minister, in the Good Officials biography.

sentences.zh: 挺幼敏寤，七歲通《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: Ting as a child was clever and understanding; at seven he mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was clever; at seven he knew the Filial Classic and Analects.

sentences.zh: 及長，有才思，好屬文，爲五言詩，善效謝康樂體。

translations.literal: When grown he had literary talent and thought, loved composition, wrote five-word poetry, and was skilled at imitating Xie Kangyue's style.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he wrote poetry in Xie Kangyue's style.

sentences.zh: 父友人樂安任昉深相歎異，常曰：「此子目下無雙。

translations.literal: His father's friend Ren Fang of Le'an deeply marveled at him and often said: "This boy under heaven has no peer."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang of Le'an often said: "This boy has no peer under heaven."

sentences.zh: 」齊末，州舉秀才，對策爲當時第一。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi the province recommended him as Outstanding Talent; in the policy response he ranked first of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's end the province recommended him as Outstanding Talent; his answers ranked first.

sentences.zh: 高祖義師至，挺迎謁於新林，高祖見之甚悅，謂曰「顏子」，引爲征東行參軍，時年十八。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army arrived, Ting went to meet and pay respects at Xinlin; Gaozu, seeing him, was very pleased and called him "Master Yan"; he was appointed Army Adjutant on the Eastern Campaign at age eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army came, Ting met him at Xinlin; Gaozu called him "Master Yan" and made him eastern-campaign adjutant at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除中軍參軍事。

translations.literal: In the early Tianjian era he was appointed Central Army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was central army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 宅居在潮溝，於宅講《論語》，聽者傾朝。

translations.literal: His residence was at Chaogou; at home he lectured on the Analects and listeners filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: At Chaogou he lectured on the Analects and the court came to listen.

sentences.zh: 遷建康正，俄以劾免。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Jiankang; soon he was dismissed after impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jiankang director, then was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，入爲尚書儀曹郎，遷西中郎記室參軍，累爲晉陵、武康令。

translations.literal: After a long while he entered the Masters of Writing as Gentleman of Ceremonies, was promoted to Western Central secretariat staff officer, and in succession was Magistrate of Jinling and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was ceremonies gentleman, western secretariat officer, then Jinling and Wukang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 罷縣還，仍於東郊築室，不復仕。

translations.literal: When he left office and returned, he still built a house in the eastern suburbs and did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he built in the eastern suburbs and never served again.

sentences.zh: 挺少有盛名，又善處當世，朝中勢素，多與交遊，故不能久事隱靜。

translations.literal: Ting from youth had great fame and was also skilled at dealing with the age; many powerful figures at court associated with him, so he could not long pursue quiet seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Famous young and skilled with power-holders, he could not stay secluded long.

sentences.zh: 時僕射徐勉以疾假還宅，挺致書以觀其意曰：

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister Xu Mian took sick leave and returned home; Ting sent a letter to test his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian took sick leave home; Ting wrote to test his mind:

sentences.zh: 昔士德懷顧，戀興數日；

translations.literal: In the past Shi De cherished his patron and yearned for the journey several days;
translations.idiomatic: Shi De once yearned for his patron several days;

sentences.zh: 輔嗣思友，情勞一旬。

translations.literal: Fusi missed his friend and was emotionally wearied for a ten-day span.
translations.idiomatic: Fusi missed a friend and was weary ten days.

sentences.zh: 故知深心所係，貴賤一也。

translations.literal: thus one knows what the deep heart is bound to does not differ between noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: so the heart's bond is the same for noble and base.

sentences.zh: 況復恩隆世親，義重知己，道庇生人，德弘覆蓋。

translations.literal: How much more when favor is lofty as a kin of the age and righteousness weighs heavy as knowing a friend—your Way shelters the living and your virtue spreads wide as cover.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when kinship and friendship weigh heavy and your virtue shelters all.

sentences.zh: 而朝野懸隔，山川邈殊，雖咳唾時沾，而顏色不覯。

translations.literal: Yet court and countryside hang apart and mountains and rivers are far and different; though your cough and spittle sometimes reach me, I do not see your face.
translations.idiomatic: Yet court and countryside are far; though your words reach me I do not see your face.

sentences.zh: 《東山》之歎，豈云旋復；

translations.literal: The sigh of the "Eastern Mountain"—can one say it will soon return?
translations.idiomatic: Can the sigh for the Eastern Mountain soon end?

sentences.zh: 西風可懷，孰能無思。

translations.literal: The west wind is worth cherishing—who can be without thought?
translations.idiomatic: Who can cherish the west wind without longing?

sentences.zh: 加以靜居廓處，顧影莫酬，秋風四起，園林易色，涼野寂寞，寒蟲吟叫。

translations.literal: Add to this dwelling quietly in an open place with no companion for one's shadow; the autumn wind rises on four sides, gardens and groves change color, the cool wilds are lonely, and cold insects cry.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet dwelling, no companion, autumn wind, gardens fade, insects cry in the cold wilds.

sentences.zh: 懷抱不可直置，情慮不能無託，時因吟詠，動輒盈篇。

translations.literal: What the bosom holds cannot be set down straight; feeling and thought cannot be without a resting place—sometimes through chanting and singing, at a move, a full scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Feelings cannot rest; he often chanted and filled scrolls.

sentences.zh: 揚生沉鬱，且猶覆盎；

translations.literal: Even Yang Sheng was sunk in gloom and still overturned the jar;
translations.idiomatic: Even Yang Sheng in gloom overturned his jar;

sentences.zh: 惠子五車，彌多踳駮。

translations.literal: Huizi's five cartloads only multiplied contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: Huizi's five cartloads only bred contradictions.

sentences.zh: 一日聊呈小文，不朞過賞，還逮隆渥，累牘兼翰，紙縟字磨，誦復無已，徒恨許與過當，有傷准的。

translations.literal: One day I casually present a small piece, not expecting excessive praise, yet you return with lofty favor, piled sheets and doubled documents, paper dense and characters worn—reading again without end; I only regret that praise exceeds the mark and harms the standard.
translations.idiomatic: I sent a small piece unexpecting praise; you returned piled papers—I fear praise exceeds the mark.

sentences.zh: 昔子建不欲妄贊陳琳，恐見嗤哂後代；

translations.literal: In the past Zijian did not wish to praise Chen Lin rashly, fearing mockery from later generations;
translations.idiomatic: Zijian feared praising Chen Lin lest later ages mock;

sentences.zh: 今之過奢餘論，將不有累清談？

translations.literal: will today's excessive leftover discourse not burden pure talk?
translations.idiomatic: will today's excess not burden pure talk?

sentences.zh: 挺竄迹草萊，事絕聞見，藉以謳謠，得之輿牧。

translations.literal: Ting hides his tracks in grass and fields, events cut off from hearing and seeing; I rely on songs and ballads and get them from cart and pasture.
translations.idiomatic: I hide in the fields and learn only from songs and herdsmen.

sentences.zh: 仰承有事砭石，仍成簡通，娛腸悅耳，稍從擯落，宴處榮觀，務在滌除。

translations.literal: Looking up I receive your active stone needle and it still becomes simple communication; pleasing the gut and delighting the ear, I slightly follow casting off; feasting in glory and view, I aim at cleansing away.
translations.idiomatic: Your sharp words please me; I cast off glory and feast to cleanse myself.

sentences.zh: 綺羅絲竹，二列頓遣；

translations.literal: Brocade, silk, and bamboo music—two rows suddenly dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Brocade and music—two rows dismissed at once;

sentences.zh: 方丈員案，三桮僅存。

translations.literal: a square zhang and round table—only three cups remain.
translations.idiomatic: a square table—only three cups remain.

sentences.zh: 故以道變區中，情沖域外；

translations.literal: thus with the Way transforming the realm within, feeling rushes beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Way transforms the realm and feeling rushes beyond it.

sentences.zh: 操彼弦誦，賁茲觀損。

translations.literal: Wielding that string and chant, I adorn this view of loss.
translations.idiomatic: I chant strings and adorn this view of loss.

sentences.zh: 追留侯之卻粒，念韓卿之辭榮；

translations.literal: I recall the Marquis of Liu declining grain and think of Minister Han resigning glory;
translations.idiomatic: I recall Liu declining grain and Han resigning glory;

sentences.zh: 眷想東都，屬懷南岳；

translations.literal: my thoughts cling to the eastern capital and my heart attaches to the southern peak;
translations.idiomatic: my thoughts cling to the eastern capital and the southern peak;

sentences.zh: 鑽仰來貺，有符下風。

translations.literal: drilling into and looking up at your coming gift, it matches the lower wind.
translations.idiomatic: your gift matches the lower wind.

sentences.zh: 雖云幸甚，然則未喻。

translations.literal: Though one says it is very fortunate, yet I am not enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortunate, I am not enlightened.

sentences.zh: 雖復帝道康寧，走馬行卻，《由庚》得所，寅亮有歸。

translations.literal: Though again the imperial Way is peaceful and horses run in retreat, "You Geng" finds its place, and Yin and Liang have where to return.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm is peaceful and Yin and Liang have where to return,

sentences.zh: 悠悠之人，展氏猶且攘袂；

translations.literal: the distant man Zhan still rolls up his sleeves;
translations.idiomatic: the distant man Zhan still rolls his sleeves;

sentences.zh: 浩浩白水，甯叟方欲褰裳。

translations.literal: the vast white waters—old Ning is about to lift his robe.
translations.idiomatic: on vast waters old Ning lifts his robe.

sentences.zh: 是知君子拯物，義非徇己。

translations.literal: thus one knows the gentleman who saves things does not act for himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: thus the gentleman saves things, not for himself alone.

sentences.zh: 思與赤松子遊，誰其克遂。

translations.literal: I think of wandering with Master Red Pine—who can achieve it?
translations.idiomatic: Who can wander with Master Red Pine?

sentences.zh: 願驅之仁壽，綏此多福。

translations.literal: May you drive them to benevolence and longevity and soothe this many blessings.
translations.idiomatic: May you drive them to benevolence and soothe many blessings.

sentences.zh: 雖則不言，四時行矣。

translations.literal: Though one does not speak, the four seasons move.
translations.idiomatic: Though silent, the four seasons move.

sentences.zh: 然後黔首有庇，薦紳靡奪；

translations.literal: Then the black-haired people have shelter and girdled gentlemen are not deprived;
translations.idiomatic: Then the people have shelter and gentlemen are not deprived;

sentences.zh: 白駒不在空谷，屠羊豫蒙其賚。

translations.literal: the white colt is not in an empty valley; the butcher's sheep also receives bounty.
translations.idiomatic: the white colt is not in an empty valley; the butcher's sheep receive bounty.

sentences.zh: 豈不休哉？

translations.literal: Is it not glorious?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not glorious?

sentences.zh: 豈不休哉？

translations.literal: Is it not glorious?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not glorious?

sentences.zh: 昔杜真自閉深室，郎宗絕迹幽野。

translations.literal: In the past Du Zhen shut himself in a deep room and Lang Zong left no tracks in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen shut himself deep; Lang Zong left no tracks in the wild.

sentences.zh: 難矣，誠非所希。

translations.literal: Hard indeed—and truly not what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Hard indeed—and not what I hope for.

sentences.zh: 井丹高潔，相如慢世，尚復遊涉權門，雍容鄉邑，常謂此道爲泰，每竊慕之。

translations.literal: Jing Dan was lofty and pure, Sima Xiangru looked down on the age—yet they still traveled among power's gates and moved at ease in home districts; I often say this Way is grand and secretly admire it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Dan and Sima Xiangru still visited power's gates—I secretly admire that grand Way.

sentences.zh: 方念擁帚延思，以陳侍者，請至農隙，無待邀求。

translations.literal: Just now I think of holding the broom to extend thought and present it to attendants; please come at the farm gap—no need to wait for invitation.
translations.idiomatic: I think of holding the broom for you—come at the farm gap without waiting.

sentences.zh: 挺誠好屬文，不會今世，不能促節局步，以應流俗。

translations.literal: Ting truly loves composition and does not meet the present age; he cannot quicken his step to answer the floating age.
translations.idiomatic: Ting loves writing but cannot quicken his step for the floating age.

sentences.zh: 事等昌菹，謬彼偏嗜，是用不羞固陋，無憚龍門。

translations.literal: The matter is like spoiled pickle; I wrongly share that partial taste—therefore I am not ashamed of my rusticity and do not fear the dragon gate.
translations.idiomatic: Like spoiled pickle I wrongly share the taste—not ashamed of rusticity, not fearing the dragon gate.

sentences.zh: 昔敬通之賞景卿，孟公之知仲蔚，止乎通人，猶稱盛美，況在時宗，彌爲未易。

translations.literal: In the past Jingtong prized Jingqing and Meng Gong knew Zhongwei—stopping at ordinary men they were still called greatly beautiful; how much more in the age's elite—it is even less easy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong prized Jingqing and Meng Gong knew Zhongwei—even among ordinary men that was beautiful; how much more among elites.

sentences.zh: 近以蒲槧勿用，箋素多闕，聊效東方，獻書丞相，須得善寫，更請潤訶，儻逢子侯，比復削牘。

translations.literal: Recently because coarse paper is not used and fine silk is much lacking, I imitate the eastern man and present a book to the chief minister; I must have a good copyist and again ask for polishing; if I meet Zihou, again I will trim the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Paper is lacking; I imitate the eastern man and present a book to the chief minister for copying and polish.

sentences.zh: 勉報曰：

translations.literal: Mian replied:
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied:

sentences.zh: 復覽來書，累牘兼翰；

translations.literal: Again I read your letter, piled sheets and doubled documents;
translations.idiomatic: Again I read your letter, piled sheets;

sentences.zh: 事苞出處，言兼語默；

translations.literal: the matter wraps emergence and withdrawal, the words join speech and silence;
translations.idiomatic: matter wraps emergence and withdrawal, words join speech and silence;

sentences.zh: 事義周悉，意致深遠；

translations.literal: the matter and meaning are thorough, the intent and reach far;
translations.idiomatic: matter and meaning thorough, intent far;

sentences.zh: 發函伸紙，倍增憤歎。

translations.literal: opening the letter and spreading the paper, it doubles indignant sighs.
translations.idiomatic: opening the letter doubles my sighs.

sentences.zh: 卿雄州擢秀，弱冠升朝，穿綜百家，佃漁六學；

translations.literal: You, a splendid shoot from a heroic province, rose to court at weak cap; you thread through a hundred schools and plow the six learnings;
translations.idiomatic: You rose at weak cap, mastered a hundred schools and six learnings;

sentences.zh: 觀眸表其韶慧，視色見其英朗，若魯國之名駒，邁雲中之白鶴。

translations.literal: looking in the eyes shows your bright wisdom, seeing the color shows his heroic clarity—like the famous colt of Lu or the white crane soaring in clouds.
translations.idiomatic: your eyes show bright wisdom, your color heroic clarity—like Lu's colt or a cloud crane.

sentences.zh: 及占顯邑，試吏腴壤，將有武城弦歌，桐鄉謠詠，豈與卓魯斷斷同年而語邪？

translations.literal: When you took charge of a famous district and tried office in fertile soil, there would be Wucheng's zither song and Tongxiang's ballad—how could one speak of them in the same breath as Zhuo and Lu?
translations.idiomatic: In a famous district you would sing like Wucheng and Tongxiang—not Zhuo and Lu.

sentences.zh: 方當見賞良能，有加寵授，飾茲簪帶，置彼周行。

translations.literal: Just now you should be rewarded for good ability and given added favor and appointment, adorning this girdle and setting you in that row of court.
translations.idiomatic: You should be rewarded and set in court's row.

sentences.zh: 而欲遠慕卷舒，用懷愚智，旣知益之爲累，爰悟滿則辭多，高蹈風塵，良所欽挹。

translations.literal: Yet you wish to admire from afar curling and stretching and use your heart for folly and wisdom; already knowing gain is a burden, then awakening that fullness brings many words—high-stepping in wind and dust is truly what I admire and draw in.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you admire curling and stretching, know gain burdens, and high-step in wind and dust—I admire that.

sentences.zh: 況以金商戒節，素秋御序，蕭條林野，無人相樂，偃臥墳籍，游浪儒玄，物我兼忘，寵辱誰滯？

translations.literal: How much more when metal and autumn warn the season and plain autumn orders the sequence—desolate woods and wilds with no one to share joy, lying on tomb classics and roaming Confucian mystery, thing and self both forgotten—who stagnates favor and disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: In desolate autumn you lie on classics and forget thing and self—who stagnates favor and disgrace?

sentences.zh: 誠乃歡羨，用有殊同。

translations.literal: Truly it is joy and admiration, with a difference in use.
translations.idiomatic: Truly joy and admiration, with a difference in use.

sentences.zh: 今逖聽傍求，興懷寤宿，白駒空穀，幽人引領，貧賤爲恥，鳥獸難羣，故當捐此薜蘿，出從鵷鷺，無乖隱顯，不亦休哉！

translations.literal: Now listening far and seeking nearby, I wake from sleep with rising thought; the white colt in the empty valley—the recluse stretches his neck; poverty and baseness are shame, birds and beasts are hard to flock with—therefore you should cast off this creeper and rushwort and go out to follow the court flock; no conflict between hidden and manifest—is it not glorious!
translations.idiomatic: The recluse stretches his neck in the empty valley—cast off creeper and follow the court flock; hidden or manifest, glorious!

sentences.zh: 吾智乏佐時，才慚濟世，稟承朝則，不敢荒寧，力弱途遙，愧心非一。

translations.literal: My wisdom lacks aiding the age, my talent shames saving the world; I receive the court's pattern and dare not be idle in peace; strength weak and road far—regret in the heart is not one.
translations.idiomatic: My wisdom lacks aiding the age; I receive the pattern and dare not be idle—regret is not one.

sentences.zh: 天下有道，堯人何事？

translations.literal: When all under Heaven has the Way, what business have Yao's people?
translations.idiomatic: When the realm has the Way, what business have Yao's people?

sentences.zh: 得因疲病，念從閒逸。

translations.literal: I may because of weariness and illness think of following leisure and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Weariness and illness make me think of leisure.

sentences.zh: 若使車書混合，尉候無警，作樂制禮，紀石封山，然後乃返服衡門，實爲多幸。

translations.literal: If carriage and script were mixed and guard posts had no alarm, making music and regulating rites, recording stone and sealing mountain—only then returning to serve at the balanced gate would truly be much fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If the realm were united and rites made, then returning to the balanced gate would be great fortune.

sentences.zh: 但夙有風咳，遘茲虛眩，瘠類士安，羸同長孺，簿領沉廢，臺閣未理，娛耳爛腸，因事而息，非關欲追松子，遠慕留侯。

translations.literal: But from old I have wind cough; I meet this empty dizziness; thin like Shi An, weak like Ji Changru; documents sink abandoned, the terrace not ordered; pleasing the ear and rotting the gut—I rest because of affairs, not because I wish to pursue Master Pine or admire the Marquis of Liu from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Wind cough and dizziness leave documents abandoned—not because I pursue Master Pine or the Marquis of Liu.

sentences.zh: 若乃天假之年，自當靖恭所職。

translations.literal: If Heaven grants years, of myself I should respectfully perform my duties.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven grants years I should perform my duties.

sentences.zh: 擬非倫匹，良覺辭費；

translations.literal: The comparison is not of the same kind—I truly feel the words excessive;
translations.idiomatic: The comparison is not of the same kind—words excessive;

sentences.zh: 覽復迴圈，爽焉如失。

translations.literal: reading again I turn in circles, refreshed as if lost.
translations.idiomatic: reading again I turn as if lost.

sentences.zh: 清塵獨遠，白雲飄蕩，依然何極。

translations.literal: Clear dust alone far, white clouds drifting—how endless it still is.
translations.idiomatic: Clear dust far, white clouds drifting—how endless.

sentences.zh: 猥降書札，示之文翰，覽復成誦，流連縟紙。

translations.literal: You condescend to lower a letter and show literary drafts; I read again and can chant, lingering on the dense paper.
translations.idiomatic: You lower a letter and show drafts; I read again and linger on the paper.

sentences.zh: 昔仲宣才敏，藉中郎而表譽；

translations.literal: In the past Zhongxuan was quick-witted and relied on the Central Commander to display praise;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan relied on the central commander for praise;

sentences.zh: 正平穎悟，賴北海以騰聲。

translations.literal: Zhengping was sharp and understanding and depended on Beihai to soar in fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengping depended on Beihai to soar in fame.

sentences.zh: 望古料今，吾有慚德。

translations.literal: Looking at antiquity and measuring today, I have shame in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at antiquity and today, I have shame in virtue.

sentences.zh: 儻成卷帙，力爲稱首。

translations.literal: If it becomes a scroll, exert yourself as chief.
translations.idiomatic: If it becomes a scroll, be chief.

sentences.zh: 無令獨耀隨掌，空使辭人扼腕。

translations.literal: Do not let a lone brilliance follow the palm and empty make men of letters wring wrists.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let lone brilliance follow the palm and make writers wring wrists.

sentences.zh: 式閭願見，宜事掃門。

translations.literal: Shilü wishes to see you—properly you should sweep the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shilü wishes to see you—you should sweep the gate.

sentences.zh: 亦有來思，赴其懸榻。

translations.literal: There is also coming thought—go to his suspended couch.
translations.idiomatic: There is also coming thought—go to his suspended couch.

sentences.zh: 輕苔魚網，別當以薦。

translations.literal: Light moss and fish nets—another time I shall present them as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Light moss and fish nets—I shall present another time.

sentences.zh: 城闕之歎，曷日無懷；

translations.literal: The sigh for city towers—on what day is there no longing?
translations.idiomatic: The sigh for city towers—when is there no longing?

sentences.zh: 所遲萱蘇，書不盡意。

translations.literal: What I delay is healing herbs; the letter does not exhaust the intent.
translations.idiomatic: What I delay is healing herbs; the letter does not exhaust intent.

sentences.zh: 挺後遂出仕，尋除南臺治書，因事納賄，當被推劾。

translations.literal: Afterward Ting then took office; soon he was appointed Director of Documents for the Southern Terrace; because of affairs he accepted bribes and was about to be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took office as southern-terrace director of documents and took bribes.

sentences.zh: 挺懼罪，遂變服爲道人，久之藏匿，後遇赦，乃出天心寺。

translations.literal: Ting feared punishment, then changed dress to become a Daoist priest, hid a long time, later met an amnesty, and only then came out of Tianxin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment he became a Daoist priest, hid, then came out after amnesty.

sentences.zh: 會邵陵王爲江州，攜挺之鎮，王好文義，深被恩禮，挺因此還俗。

translations.literal: When Prince Shaoling was in Jiangzhou he took Ting to the post; the prince loved literary meaning and deeply showed favor and courtesy; Ting therefore returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoling took him to Jiangzhou, favored him, and he returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 復隨王遷鎮郢州，徵入爲京尹，挺留夏首，久之還京師。

translations.literal: Again he followed the prince when he moved to post at Yingzhou; summoned to be Capital Intendant, Ting stayed at Xiashou; after a long while he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince to Yingzhou; summoned as capital intendant he stayed at Xiashou, then returned.

sentences.zh: 太清中，客游吳興、吳郡，侯景亂中卒。

translations.literal: In the Taiping era he traveled as guest in Wuxing and Wu commanderies and died in the Hou Jing rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping he traveled Wuxing and Wu and died in Hou Jing's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 著《邇說》十卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Near Discourses in ten juan and collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Near Discourses (10 j.) and collected writings (20 j.).

sentences.zh: 子知命，先隨挺事邵陵王，掌書記。

translations.literal: His son Zhiming first followed Ting in serving Prince Shaoling and managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhiming served Prince Shaoling and managed documents.

sentences.zh: 亂中，王於郢州奔敗，知命仍下投侯景。

translations.literal: In the rebellion when the prince was defeated at Yingzhou, Zhiming still went down to join Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In rebellion when the prince was defeated at Yingzhou, Zhiming joined Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 常以其父宦途不至，深怨朝廷，遂盡心事景。

translations.literal: He always because his father's official path did not reach high rank deeply resented the court, and thereupon devoted himself wholly to Jing's service.
translations.idiomatic: He resented the court for his father's low rank and wholly served Jing.

sentences.zh: 景襲郢州，圍巴陵，軍中書檄，皆其文也。

translations.literal: When Jing attacked Yingzhou and besieged Baling, all military proclamations in the army were his writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing besieged Baling, army proclamations were his writing.

sentences.zh: 及景篡位，爲中書舍人，專任權寵，勢傾內外。

translations.literal: When Jing usurped the throne he was Secretariat Attendant, solely wielding favor and power, his influence tilting inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing usurped he was secretariat attendant with power inside and out.

sentences.zh: 景敗被執，送江陵，於獄中幽死。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated he was seized and sent to Jiangling and died secretly in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell he was sent to Jiangling and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 挺弟捶，亦有才名，先爲邵陵王所引，歷爲記室、中記室、參軍。

translations.literal: Ting's younger brother Chui also had literary fame; earlier he was drawn in by Prince Shaoling and in succession was secretariat, central secretariat, and staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Chui also had fame and was Shaoling's secretariat and staff officer.

sentences.zh: 庾仲容字仲容，潁川觌焉陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongrong, courtesy name Zhongrong, was a man of Guyanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongrong, styled Zhongrong, was from Guyanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 晉司空冰六代孫。

translations.literal: Sixth-generation descendant of Jin Director of Works Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-generation descendant of Jin director of works Bing.

sentences.zh: 祖徽之，宋御史中丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huizhi was Song Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huizhi served Song as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 父漪，齊邵陵王記室。

translations.literal: His father Yi was recorder for the Prince of Shaoling of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was Qi recorder for the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 仲容幼孤，爲叔父泳所養。

translations.literal: Zhongrong was orphaned young and was raised by his uncle Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Zhongrong was raised by his uncle Yong.

sentences.zh: 旣長，杜絕人事，專精篤學，晝夜手不輟卷。

translations.literal: When grown he shut out worldly affairs, studied with single devotion, and day and night never set his books aside.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he shut out the world, studied devotedly, and never put his books down day or night.

sentences.zh: 初爲安西法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He first served as acting Army Adjutant in the Anxi Command.
translations.idiomatic: He began as acting army adjutant in the Anxi command.

sentences.zh: 泳時已貴顯，吏部尚書徐勉擬泳子晏嬰爲宮僚，泳垂泣曰：「兄子幼孤，人才粗可，願以晏嬰所忝回用之。

translations.literal: Yong was already eminent; Minister of Personnel Xu Mian proposed Yong's son Yan Ying for palace staff, and Yong wept and said: "My elder brother's son is young and orphaned; his talent is passable—I beg that what Yan Ying would receive be turned to him instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was already eminent; Xu Mian as minister of personnel proposed Yong's son Yan Ying for palace staff; Yong wept: "My brother's orphaned son has passable talent—please give Yan Ying's post to him instead.

sentences.zh: 」勉許焉，因轉仲容爲太子舍人。

translations.literal: " Mian agreed, and Zhongrong was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " Mian agreed and made Zhongrong crown prince attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷安成王主簿。

translations.literal: He was moved to secretary to the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He became secretary to the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 時平原劉孝標亦爲府佐，並以強學爲王所禮接。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan was also on the princely staff; both were honored by the prince for their forceful learning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan was also on the staff; both were honored for forceful learning.

sentences.zh: 遷晉安功曹史。

translations.literal: He was moved to merit-clerk of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jin'an merit-clerk.

sentences.zh: 歷爲永康、錢唐、武康令，治縣並無異績，多被劾。

translations.literal: He served in turn as magistrate of Yongkang, Qiantang, and Wukang; in governing the counties he showed no special achievement and was often impeached.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yongkang, Qiantang, and Wukang with no notable achievement and was often impeached.

sentences.zh: 久之，除安成王中記室，當出隨府，皇太子以舊恩，特降餞宴，賜詩曰：「孫生陟陽道，吳子朝歌縣。

translations.literal: After long service he was made the Prince of Ancheng's senior recorder; when he was to leave with the princely establishment the crown prince, out of old favor, specially held a farewell feast and bestowed a poem: "Master Sun climbed the Yang Road; Master Wu went to Chaoge county.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he became the Prince of Ancheng's senior recorder; leaving with the prince, the crown prince held a farewell feast and gave a poem: "Master Sun climbed the Yang Road; Master Wu went to Chaoge county.

sentences.zh: 未若樊林舉，置酒臨華殿。

translations.literal: Not like raising cups in Fan Forest, setting wine before Hua Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Not like raising wine in Fan Forest before Hua Palace."

sentences.zh: 」時輩榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the time took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 遷安西武陵王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to consulting adjutant to the Anxi Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He became consulting adjutant to the Anxi Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 除尚書左丞，坐推糾不直免。

translations.literal: He was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and dismissed for improper impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Made left vice director of the secretariat, he was dismissed for improper impeachment.

sentences.zh: 仲容博學，少有盛名，頗任氣使酒，好危言高論，士友以此少之。

translations.literal: Zhongrong was broadly learned and had early fame; he was quite willful and fond of wine, loved startling words and lofty talk—scholar friends thought less of him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong was learned and famed early but willful and fond of wine, loved bold talk, and friends thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 唯與王籍、謝幾卿情好相得，二人時亦不調，遂相追隨，誕縱酣飲，不復持檢操。

translations.literal: Only with Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing was he truly close; they too were unrestrained, followed one another in wild drinking, and no longer kept restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Ji and Xie Jiqing were close; all three were unrestrained, drank wildly together, and abandoned propriety.

sentences.zh: 久之，復爲諮議參軍，出爲黟縣令。

translations.literal: After long time he was again consulting adjutant and went out as magistrate of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again consulting adjutant and went out as magistrate of Yi.

sentences.zh: 及太清亂，客遊會稽，遇疾卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: When the Taiping turmoil came he was traveling in Kuaiji, fell ill, and died at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiping turmoil he was traveling in Kuaiji, fell ill, and died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 仲容抄諸子書三十卷，衆家地理書二十卷，《列女傳》三卷，文集二十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: Zhongrong abridged Masters texts in thirty juan, collected geography books in twenty juan, Biographies of Exemplary Women in three juan, and a literary collection in twenty juan—all circulated.
translations.idiomatic: He abridged masters in thirty juan, geography in twenty, Exemplary Women in three, and a collection in twenty—all circulated.

sentences.zh: 陸雲公字子龍，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Yungong, styled Zilong, was a man of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yungong, styled Zilong, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖閑，州別駕。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian was provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian was a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 父完，寧遠長史。

translations.literal: His father Wan was chief clerk of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan was Ningyuan chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 雲公五歲誦《論語》、《毛詩》，九歲讀《漢書》，略能記憶。

translations.literal: At five Yungong could recite the Analects and Mao Odes; at nine he read the Book of Han and could mostly remember it.
translations.idiomatic: At five he recited the Analects and Mao Odes; at nine he read the Book of Han and remembered most of it.

sentences.zh: 從祖倕、沛國劉顯質問十事，雲公對無所失，顯歎異之。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Tong and Liu Xian of Peiguo tested him on ten points; Yungong answered without fail and Xian marveled.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Tong and Liu Xian of Peiguo tested him on ten points; he missed none and Xian marveled.

sentences.zh: 旣長，好學有才思。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and had talent.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning and had talent.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province nominated him Presented Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him presented scholar.

sentences.zh: 累遷宣惠武陵王、平西湘東王行參軍。

translations.literal: He rose through posts as acting staff officer to the Xuanhui Prince of Wuling and the Pingxi Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose as acting staff officer to the Xuanhui Prince of Wuling and the Pingxi Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 雲公先制《太伯廟碑》，吳興太守張纘罷郡經途，讀其文歎曰：「今之蔡伯喈也。

translations.literal: Yungong had earlier composed "Memorial Stele for the Grand Duke Temple"; Zhang Zuan, ending his term as Wuxing governor, passed by, read it, and sighed: "Today's Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong had written the Grand Duke Temple stele; Zhang Zuan, leaving Wuxing, read it and sighed: "Today's Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 」纘至都掌選，言之於高祖，召兼尚書儀曹郎，頃之即真，入直壽光省，以本官知著作郎事。

translations.literal: " Zuan reached the capital in charge of selection, spoke of him to Gaozu, and Yungong was summoned as acting Director of Ritual in the Secretariat; soon confirmed, he entered duty at Shouguang Hall and with his title oversaw the Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan reached the capital, spoke to Gaozu, and Yungong was summoned as acting ritual director, soon confirmed, entered Shouguang duty, and oversaw the historiographer.

sentences.zh: 俄除著作郎，累遷中書黃門郎，並掌著作。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Historiographer, rose to Secretariat Gentleman, and held historiography as well.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made historiographer, he rose to secretariat gentleman and kept historiography.

sentences.zh: 雲公善弈棊，嘗夜侍御坐，武冠觸燭火，高祖笑謂曰：「燭燒卿貂。

translations.literal: Yungong was skilled at weiqi; once at night attending the imperial seat his warrior cap touched a candle flame and Gaozu laughed and said: "The lamp burns your marten.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was skilled at weiqi; once at night on imperial duty his cap touched a candle and Gaozu laughed: "The lamp burns your marten.

sentences.zh: 」高祖將用雲公爲侍中，故以此言戲之也。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was about to use Yungong as Palace Attendant—that is why he joked thus.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu was about to make him palace attendant—that is why he joked.

sentences.zh: 是時天淵池新制鯿魚舟，形闊而短，高祖暇日，常汎此舟，在朝唯引太常劉之遴、國子祭酒到溉、右衛朱异，雲公時年位尚輕，亦預焉。

translations.literal: Then the new bream-boat on Tianyuan Pool was broad and short; on leisure days Gaozu would float it, inviting only Liu Zhiliao as Grand Chamberlain, Dao Gai as Chancellor of the National University, and Zhu Yi as Right Guard—and Yungong, still young in years and rank, also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Then the new bream-boat on Tianyuan Pool was broad and short; on leisure days Gaozu floated it with only Liu Zhiliao, Dao Gai, and Zhu Yi—and Yungong, still young, also came.

sentences.zh: 其恩遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his favor.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，卒，時年三十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taqing he died at age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Taqing year one he died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 高祖悼惜之，手詔曰：「給事黃門侍郎、掌著作陸雲公，風尚優敏，後進之秀。
