translations.literal: Gaozu mourned him and wrote in his own hand: "Palace Attendant and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, in charge of historiography Lu Yungong—bearing refined and keen, a rising talent of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him and wrote: "Palace attendant and historiography chief Lu Yungong—refined and keen, a rising talent.

sentences.zh: 奄然殂謝，良以惻然。

translations.literal: Suddenly gone—truly grievous.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly gone—deeply grievous.

sentences.zh: 可剋日舉哀，賻錢五萬、布四十匹。」

translations.literal: Let mourning be held on an appointed day; grant funeral money fifty thousand and forty bolts of cloth."
translations.idiomatic: Hold mourning on an appointed day; grant fifty thousand cash and forty bolts of cloth."

sentences.zh: 張纘時爲湘州，與雲公叔襄、兄晏子書曰：「都信至，承賢兄子賢弟黃門殞折，非唯貴門喪寶，實有識同悲，痛惋傷惜，不能已已。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan was then in Xiangzhou and wrote to Yungong's uncle Xiang and elder brother Yanzi: "The capital messenger has come; I learn that your worthy nephew and worthy younger brother the Yellow Gate Gentleman has perished—not only your house has lost a treasure; men of insight share the grief; pain and regret will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan in Xiangzhou wrote Yungong's uncle Xiang and brother Yanzi: "The capital messenger came; your worthy nephew and brother the Yellow Gate Gentleman has died—not only your house loses a treasure; the knowing grieve with you; pain will not cease.

sentences.zh: 賢兄子賢弟神情早著，標令弱年，經目所睹，殆無再問。

translations.literal: Your worthy nephew and younger brother showed spirit early; even in tender years what he saw needed scarcely be asked again.
translations.idiomatic: Your nephew and brother showed spirit early; in youth what he saw needed scarcely be asked again.

sentences.zh: 懷橘抱柰，稟自天情；

translations.literal: Holding oranges and embracing apple trees came from inborn feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Holding oranges and embracing trees came from inborn feeling;

sentences.zh: 倨坐列薪，非因外獎。

translations.literal: sitting upright amid firewood was not from outward praise.
translations.idiomatic: sitting upright amid firewood was not from outward praise.

sentences.zh: 學以聚之，則一箸能立；

translations.literal: Gather learning and one chopstick can stand;
translations.idiomatic: Gather learning and one chopstick can stand;

sentences.zh: 問以辯之，則師心獨寤。

translations.literal: question to clarify and the teacher in the heart alone awakens.
translations.idiomatic: question to clarify and the heart alone awakens.

sentences.zh: 始逾弱歲，辭藝通洽，升降多士，秀也詩流。

translations.literal: Just past tender years his letters and arts were thorough; among many scholars he was the outstanding stream of poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Just past tender years his letters and arts were thorough; among scholars he was poetry's outstanding stream.

sentences.zh: 見與齒過肩隨，禮殊拜絕，懷抱相得，忘其年義。

translations.literal: When we met we passed shoulder to shoulder; courtesy set aside bowing and parting; our hearts matched and we forgot the years between us.
translations.idiomatic: We met passing shoulder to shoulder; courtesy set aside formal bows; our hearts matched and we forgot the years between us.

sentences.zh: 朝遊夕宴，一載于斯；

translations.literal: Morning outings and evening feasts lasted a full year;
translations.idiomatic: Morning outings and evening feasts lasted a full year;

sentences.zh: 翫古披文，終晨訖暮。

translations.literal: delighting in antiquity and unfolding texts from dawn to dusk.
translations.idiomatic: delighting in antiquity and unfolding texts from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 平生知舊，零落稍盡，老夫記意，其數幾何。

translations.literal: Friends of a lifetime have mostly fallen away; what the old man remembers counts how many?
translations.idiomatic: Friends of a lifetime have mostly fallen away; what the old man remembers—how many?

sentences.zh: 至若此生，寧可多過，賞心樂事，所寄伊人。

translations.literal: As for this life, could there be many more? Joy of heart and pleasure of affairs were entrusted to one man alone.
translations.idiomatic: As for this life, could there be many more? Heart's joy was entrusted to one man alone.

sentences.zh: 弟遷職瀟、湘，維舟洛汭，將離之際，彌見情款。

translations.literal: When you moved to Xiao and Xiang you moored at Luoyang's bend; at the moment of parting affection showed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When you moved to Xiao and Xiang you moored at Luoyang's bend; at parting affection deepened.

sentences.zh: 夕次帝郊，亟淹信宿，徘徊握手，忍分歧路。

translations.literal: One evening we stopped at the imperial suburb and lingered two nights; hand in hand we lingered, unwilling to split the road.
translations.idiomatic: One evening we stopped at the imperial suburb and lingered two nights; hand in hand we lingered, unwilling to part.

sentences.zh: 行役數年，羈病侵迫，識慮惛怳，久絕人世。

translations.literal: Years on service, illness pressing in exile—thought dulled and long cut off from the world.
translations.idiomatic: Years on service, illness in exile—thought dulled and long cut off from the world.

sentences.zh: 憑几口授，素無其功；

translations.literal: Dictated at the mouth, I had no skill at it;
translations.idiomatic: Dictated at the mouth, I had no skill;

sentences.zh: 翰動若飛，彌有多愧。

translations.literal: the brush moved like flight—how much the more ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: the brush moved like flight—all the more ashamed.

sentences.zh: 京洛游故，咸成雲雨，唯有此生，音塵數嗣。

translations.literal: Old friends of the capital have all scattered like clouds and rain; only this life kept letters many times over.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends of the capital have scattered like clouds and rain; only this life kept letters many times.

sentences.zh: 形迹之外，不爲遠近隔情；

translations.literal: Beyond form and trace, distance did not divide feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond form and trace, distance did not divide feeling;

sentences.zh: 襟素之中，豈以風霜改節？

translations.literal: within the breast's plain cloth, how could wind and frost change constancy?
translations.idiomatic: within the plain breast, how could wind and frost change constancy?

sentences.zh: 客游半紀，志切首丘，日望東歸，更敦昔款。

translations.literal: Half a decade as a traveler, heart set on returning home, day by day looking east, again deepening old affection.
translations.idiomatic: Half a decade traveling, heart set on returning home, day by day looking east, again deepening old affection.

sentences.zh: 如何此別，永成異世！

translations.literal: How can this parting be forever a different world!
translations.idiomatic: How can this parting be forever a different world!

sentences.zh: 揮袂之初，人誰自保，但恐衰謝，無復前朞。

translations.literal: At the first wave of the sleeve, who can be sure of himself? I only fear decline and that there will be no former day again.
translations.idiomatic: At the first wave of the sleeve, who can be sure? I only fear decline and no former day again.

sentences.zh: 不謂華齡，方春掩質，埋玉之恨，撫事多情。

translations.literal: I did not expect flowering years, spring just come, to hide the substance—grief at burying jade touches every affair with feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect flowering years in spring to hide the substance—grief at burying jade touches every affair.

sentences.zh: 想引進之情，懷抱素篤，友于之至，兼深家寶。

translations.literal: I think of the affection of those who brought him forward—hearts were always deep; brotherly feeling to the utmost, and also a deep family treasure.
translations.idiomatic: I think of those who brought him forward—affection always deep; brotherly feeling utmost, and also a deep family treasure.

sentences.zh: 奄有此恤，當何可言！

translations.literal: Suddenly this bereavement—what can be said!
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly this bereavement—what can be said!

sentences.zh: 臨白增悲，言以無次。」

translations.literal: Writing at parting adds grief; the words are out of order."
translations.idiomatic: Writing at parting adds grief; the words are out of order."

sentences.zh: 雲公從兄才子，亦有才名，歷官中書郎、宣成王友、太子中庶子、廷尉卿，先雲公卒。

translations.literal: Yungong's cousin Caizi also had literary fame, served as Director of the Palace Secretariat, Friend of Prince Xuancheng, Crown Prince Household Vice-Governor, and Minister of Justice, and died before Yungong.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Caizi also had literary fame, reached director of the palace secretariat, friend of Prince Xuancheng, crown prince vice-governor, and minister of justice, and died before Yungong.

sentences.zh: 才子、雲公文集，並行於世。

translations.literal: Caizi's and Yungong's collected works both circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Caizi's and Yungong's collections both circulated.

sentences.zh: 任孝恭字孝恭，臨淮臨淮人也。

translations.literal: Ren Xiaogong, styled Xiaogong, was a man of Linhuai in Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiaogong, styled Xiaogong, came from Linhuai in Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖農夫，宋南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Nongfu was Song Governor of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Nongfu was Song governor of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝恭幼孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xiaogong was orphaned young and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Xiaogong was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 精力勤學，家貧無書，常崎嶇從人假借。

translations.literal: He studied energetically; the family was poor and had no books, so he often traveled hard paths to borrow from others.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard; the family was poor and bookless, so he often traveled hard paths to borrow.

sentences.zh: 每讀一遍，諷誦略無所遺。

translations.literal: Each book he read once he could chant back with almost nothing lost.
translations.idiomatic: Each book read once he could chant back with almost nothing lost.

sentences.zh: 外祖丘它，與高祖有舊，高祖聞其有才學，召入西省撰史。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Qiu Ta had old ties with Gaozu; Gaozu heard of his talent and summoned him to the Western Secretariat to compile history.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal grandfather Qiu Ta had old ties with Gaozu; hearing of his talent, Gaozu summoned him to the Western Secretariat to compile history.

sentences.zh: 初爲奉朝請，進直壽光省，爲司文侍郎，俄兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He began as Court Gentleman, advanced to Shouguang duty as Vice Director of Literary Affairs, and soon also Secretariat Communications Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as court gentleman, advanced to Shouguang as vice director of literary affairs, and soon also secretariat communications attendant.

sentences.zh: 敕遣制《建陵寺刹下銘》，又啓撰高祖集序文，並富麗，自是專掌公家筆翰。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compose the inscription under the stupa at Jianling Temple and to draft the preface to Gaozu's collected works—both sumptuous; from then he alone managed official brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to write the Jianling stupa inscription and Gaozu's collected-works preface—both sumptuous—he alone managed official brushwork thereafter.

sentences.zh: 孝恭爲文敏速，受詔立成，若不留意，每奏，高祖輒稱善，累賜金帛。

translations.literal: Xiaogong wrote swiftly; given an edict he finished on the spot as if without effort; every memorial Gaozu praised and repeatedly gave gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong wrote swiftly; given an edict he finished on the spot; every memorial Gaozu praised and gave gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 孝恭少從蕭寺雲法師讀經論，明佛理，至是，蔬食持戒，信受甚篤。

translations.literal: In youth he had studied sutra treatises under Master Yun of Xiao Temple and understood Buddhist doctrine; by then he ate vegetables, kept precepts, and believed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied sutras under Master Yun of Xiao Temple; by then he ate vegetables, kept precepts, and believed deeply.

sentences.zh: 而性頗自伐，以才能尚人，於時輩中多有忽略，世以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he rather boasted himself, looked down on others for talent, and often neglected his contemporaries—the age thought less of him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he boasted himself, looked down on others, and often neglected contemporaries—the age thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，侯景寇逼，孝恭啓募兵，隸蕭正德，屯南岸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taqing, Hou Jing pressed the capital; Xiaogong petitioned to raise troops under Xiao Zhengde and encamped on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: In Taqing year two Hou Jing pressed the capital; Xiaogong raised troops under Xiao Zhengde on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 及賊至，正德舉衆入賊，孝恭還赴臺，臺門已閉，因奔入東府，尋爲賊所攻，城陷見害。

translations.literal: When the rebels came Zhengde led his host to join them; Xiaogong returned to the terrace but the gate was closed, fled into the Eastern Palace, and was killed when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came Zhengde joined them; Xiaogong returned to the terrace but the gate was closed, fled to the Eastern Palace, and was killed when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works circulated.

sentences.zh: 協幼孤，養於舅氏。

translations.literal: Xie was orphaned young and raised by his mother's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Xie was raised by his mother's clan.

sentences.zh: 少以器局見稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was praised for bearing and measure.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was praised for bearing and measure.

sentences.zh: 博涉羣書，工於草隸。

translations.literal: He read widely and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 釋褐湘東王國常侍，又兼府記室。

translations.literal: On first appointment he was Gentleman of the Prince of Xiangdong's state and also staff recorder.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment he was gentleman of the Prince of Xiangdong's state and also staff recorder.

sentences.zh: 世祖出鎮荊州，轉正記室。

translations.literal: When Shizu went out to govern Jingzhou he became chief recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu governed Jingzhou he became chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 時吳郡顧協亦在蕃邸，與協同名，才學相亞，府中稱爲「二協」。

translations.literal: Gu Xie of Wu commandery was also at the princely residence; same name as Xie and near in talent—the headquarters called them "the two Xies."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xie of Wu was also at the princely residence; same name and near in talent—they were called "the two Xies."

sentences.zh: 舅陳郡謝暕卒，協以有鞠養恩，居喪如伯叔之禮，議者重焉。

translations.literal: His uncle by marriage Xie Yan of Chen commandery died; Xie, having rearing grace, observed mourning like a nephew to an uncle, and critics respected it.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle by marriage Xie Yan of Chen died; Xie, having rearing grace, mourned like a nephew to an uncle, and critics respected it.

sentences.zh: 又感家門事義，不求顯達，恒辭徵辟，游於蕃府而已。

translations.literal: Moved too by the family's moral misfortune, he sought no prominence, always declining summons, remaining only at the princely house.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the family's moral misfortune, he sought no prominence, always declining summons, remaining only at the princely house.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he died at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year five he died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚嘆惜之，爲《懷舊詩》以傷之。

translations.literal: Shizu deeply mourned him and composed "Poem of Remembering the Past" to grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu deeply mourned him and wrote "Poem of Remembering the Past" to grieve.

sentences.zh: 其一章曰：「弘都多雅度，信乃含賓實。

translations.literal: One stanza says: "Hongdu has much elegant breadth; trust indeed holds guest substance.
translations.idiomatic: One stanza says: "Hongdu has much elegant breadth; trust indeed holds guest substance.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸殊未昇，上才淹下秩。」

translations.literal: The wild goose has not yet risen high; fine talent is submerged in low rank."
translations.idiomatic: The wild goose has not yet risen high; fine talent is submerged in low rank."

sentences.zh: 協所撰《晉仙傳》五篇、《日月災異圖》兩卷，遇火湮滅。

translations.literal: Xie's Five Treatises on Jin Immortals and two juan of solar-lunar portents were lost in fire.
translations.idiomatic: His Five Treatises on Jin Immortals and two juan of solar-lunar portents were lost in fire.

sentences.zh: 有二子：之儀、之推，並早知名。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Zhiyi and Zhitui, both early known.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Zhiyi and Zhitui, both early known.

sentences.zh: 之推，承聖中仕至正員郎、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zhitui during Chengsheng rose to Regular Gentleman and Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui during Chengsheng rose to regular gentleman and secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：魏文帝稱古之文人，鮮能以名節自全。

translations.literal: Yao Cha of Chen, Minister of Personnel, said: Emperor Wen of Wei said ancient men of letters rarely kept reputation and integrity intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha of Chen, minister of personnel, said: Emperor Wen of Wei said ancient men of letters rarely kept reputation and integrity intact.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫文者妙發性靈，獨拔懷抱，易邈等夷，必興矜露。

translations.literal: Writing stirs one's nature to spirit and lifts the breast alone; easy to overlook equals, it always breeds display.
translations.idiomatic: Writing stirs nature to spirit and lifts the breast alone; overlooking equals, it always breeds display.

sentences.zh: 大則淩慢侯王，小則慠蔑朋黨；

translations.literal: Greatly they insult lords and kings; in small things they scorn their circle;
translations.idiomatic: Greatly they insult lords and kings; in small things they scorn their circle;

sentences.zh: 速忌離訧，啓自此作。

sentences.zh: 若夫屈、賈之流斥，桓、馮之擯放，豈獨一世哉？

translations.literal: Qu Yuan and Jia Yi were driven off; Huan Tan and Feng Yan were cast out—was it only one age?

sentences.zh: 蓋恃才之禍也。

translations.literal: It is the disaster of relying on talent.
translations.idiomatic: It is the disaster of relying on talent.

sentences.zh: 羣士值文明之運，摛豔藻之辭，無郁抑之虞，不遭向時之患，美矣。

translations.literal: These gentlemen met a civilizing age and spread ornate phrasing; they had no depression or woes and did not suffer former ills—beautiful indeed.
translations.idiomatic: These gentlemen met a civilizing age and spread ornate phrasing; they had no depression and did not suffer former ills—beautiful indeed.

sentences.zh: 劉氏之論，命之徒也。

translations.literal: Liu's discourse is a disciple of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu's discourse is a disciple of fate.

sentences.zh: 命也者，聖人罕言歟，就而必之，非經意也。

translations.literal: Fate is what sages rarely discuss; to insist on it from their words is not what the classics mean.
